label: S0083
statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Exact negation and unbounded good indices for fixed-pair (40a)). Fix admissible (s,A), and for each M,c,d define G_{M,c,d}={m∈N: S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d}. The negation of (40a), written ∀M∀c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d], is exactly ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]; equivalently, some G_{M,c,d} is unbounded. Proof: Negate the displayed formula, reversing its quantifiers in order: ∃M∃c,d∃m0∀m≥m0 ¬[S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d]. De Morgan’s law and the linear order on resource values give the equivalent tail-bounded statement ∃M∃c,d∃m0∀m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. Therefore the negation of (40a) is the negation of this tail-bounded statement, namely ∀M∀c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d]. Conversely, negating that last formula yields ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. For a fixed M,c,d, ∀m0∃m≥m0 with m∈G is precisely that G is unbounded in N. Hence failure of (40a) means some machine and fixed exponents meet both bounds at arbitrarily large indices, not necessarily at every index beyond a threshold. This proves the exact quantifier consequence and rules out substituting an eventual-tail bound for it.

statement: statement_start: REPAIR (Exact negation of fixed-pair (40a)). Fix an admissible pair (s,A), and put P(M,c,d,m0,m):= [m≥m0 ⇒ (S_M(m)>s(m)^c ∨ τ_M(m)>s(m)^d)]. The fixed-pair assertion (40a) is ∀M∈M_{s,A}^{plain} ∀c,d ∃m0 ∀m P(M,c,d,m0,m). Its negation is exactly ∃M∈M_{s,A}^{plain} ∃c,d ∀m0 ∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. This says nothing about an eventual tail: for example G={even natural numbers} is unbounded but every tail also contains an odd number, so G contains no tail. statement: L1-fixed-s: For fixed s >= 0 and N = 2^n, let Im_s be the set of truth tables of nodes of circuits with at most s fan-in-2 gates over {x_1..x_n, 0, 1} using any of the 16 binary operations. Then |Im_s| <= (s+1)(n+s+2)·16^s·(n+s+2)^{2s}, and for each prefix length k the set {f|_[k] : f in Im_s} is computable in time |Im_s|·poly(N). Proof: at step j there are at most n+2+j earlier nodes, so there are at most (n+s+2)^{2t}·16^t circuits with t <= s gates; each circuit has at most n+s+2 nodes; summing over t = 0..s gives the bound. Scope: fixed s, all n. The per-bit cost is n^{O(s)}, so this does NOT give the poly(s,n) update needed for G0003/G0004.

statement: LEMMA L-PAT (pattern obstruction; CLAIMED until reviewed). Let n>=1, m>=n+1, W in Z^{m x n} of rank d<=n, t in Z^m, g_j(x)=[w_j.x>=t_j]. (a) The number of distinct patterns P(x)=(g_1(x),...,g_m(x)) over x in {0,1}^n is at most N(m,d)=sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF (a): factor W=PQ with Q in R^{d x n}, so w_j.x=p_j.y with y=Qx in R^d, and Y={Qx : x in {0,1}^n} is finite. Let eps>0 be smaller than every nonzero |p_j.y-t_j| (y in Y), and put h_j(y)=p_j.y-t_j+eps. Then h_j(y) is never 0 on Y and g_j(x)=[h_j(Qx)>0]. Each pattern is the sign vector of the h_j at a point of Y, so distinct patterns lie in distinct regions of the arrangement {h_j=0} in R^d. An arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^d has at most sum_{i<=d} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943; Cover 1965). (b) For d=n: N(m,n) > 2^n. PROOF (b): if m=n+1 then N=2^{n+1}-1 > 2^n since n>=1. If n+2<=m<=2n-1 then floor(m/2)<=n, and by symmetry of binomial coefficients sum_{i<=floor(m/2)} C(m,i) >= 2^{m-1} >= 2^{n+1} > 2^n. If m>=2n then N >= C(m,n)+1 >= C(2n,n)+1 > 2^n, using monotonicity of C(m,n) in m, C(2n,n)=2 (n=1), 6 (n=2), and for n>=3 C(2n,n) >= 4^n/(2n+1) >= 2^n because 2^n >= 2n+1. (c) For d<n: N(m,d) >= C(m,d) >= (m/d)^d, so N(m,d) < 2^{(1-delta)n} forces d*log2(m/d) < (1-delta)n. For m=n^{1.5} this forces d=O(n/log n), consistent with G0006. SCOPE: exact, every n>=1, m>=n+1, every integer W and t. This is a LIMIT on the class of procedures whose state is the realised bottom pattern. It is not an algorithm, and it does not close G0001.

statement: lemma,RestrictedTopSupportAlgorithm,Let f(x) = [∑_{j=1}^m v_j [W_j·x ≥ t_j] ≥ T] be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates. Suppose: (1) the top gate has at most k nonzero weights: |{j : v_j ≠ 0}| ≤ k; (2) the bottom weights are bounded integers: |W_j[i]| ≤ B for all j, i. Then #SAT(f) can be computed in time O(n k (2Bn+1)^k · poly(m)).,Proof: Let S = {j : v_j ≠ 0}, |S| = k. The function f depends on x only through the k bottom gate outputs g_S(x) = ([W_j·x ≥ t_j])_{j∈S}. For each fixed s ∈ {0,1}^k, the top gate evaluates to a constant c(s) = [∑_{j∈S} v_j s_j ≥ T]. The number of x with g_S(x) = s is the number of solutions to the system of k threshold inequalities: for j∈S, W_j·x ≥ t_j if s_j = 1, and W_j·x ≤ t_j − 1 if s_j = 0. Each linear form W_j·x takes values in [−Bn, Bn] (since |W_j[i]| ≤ B and x_i ∈ {0,1}), so at most 2Bn+1 integer values. A dynamic program over the n variables counts solutions: state = (c_1,…,c_k) ∈ [−Bn,Bn]^k, representing the current values of the k linear forms. Start with count 1 at (0,…,0). For each variable x_i = 0,1, update the counts by adding W_j[i] to c_j. The number of states is at most (2Bn+1)^k. Each update takes O(k (2Bn+1)^k) time. After n variables, for each s ∈ {0,1}^k with c(s)=1, sum the counts of states satisfying c_j ≥ t_j (s_j=1) or c_j ≤ t_j−1 (s_j=0). Total time O(n k (2Bn+1)^k + 2^k poly(k)) = O(n k (2Bn+1)^k · poly(m)). This is a proved running time for the stated restricted subclass.,kind,ALGORITHM,closes,G0011

label: S0002
statement: Verifier decision lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1, f in {0,1}^N. Let V(f,C)=1 iff C is a fan-in-2 circuit on n inputs of size <= s computing f. Let decode map an L-bit string to a circuit or to reject. Define Dec(f)=V(f, decode(S(f))). If S is correct on members (f has a size-<=s circuit implies S(f) encodes one), then Dec(f)=MCSP[s](f) for all f. Proof: member case: S(f) encodes a valid circuit, so V=1. Non-member case: no size-<=s circuit computes f, so V=0 for every string, hence Dec=0. E2 is not used. OPEN (gap): the size of V must be N*(log N)^{O(1)} to be harmless against the N(log N)^k target; only poly(N,s) overhead is shown.

label: S0003
statement: Sized verifier lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1. Encode a fan-in-2 circuit C on n inputs with s gates as L = O(s log(n+s)) bits: each gate stores two operand indices in [0, n+s) plus a gate-type bit. Let V(f,y) be the circuit with inputs f in {0,1}^N and y in {0,1}^L that outputs 1 iff y is well-formed, decodes to a circuit C of size <= s on n inputs, and C(a)=f(a) for all a in {0,1}^n. Claim: V has size O(N*s*max(n,s)). Proof: (i) Well-formedness and decoding of y cost O(L log L) gates, which is negligible. (ii) For each of the N points a, evaluate C(a) with a universal evaluator. Keep a value bank of n+s wires (the n inputs, hard-wired as constants for a, plus the s gate outputs). Gate t computes its two operands by multiplexers over the n+s bank wires, costing O(n+s) gates per operand, then one gate. One point costs O(s*(n+s)) gates. (iii) Compare C(a) with f(a): O(1) per point. Total O(N*(s*(n+s)+1)) = O(N*s*max(n,s)). With n = log N and s <= (log N)^c for a fixed c >= 1, this is O(N*(log N)^{2c}) = N*(log N)^{O(1)}. Consequence: if a search circuit S of size N(log N)^k outputs encodings of size-<=s circuits, then Dec(f)=V(f,S(f)) is a decision circuit of size N(log N)^{k'} with k' = max(k,2c)+O(1). By S0002, Dec = MCSP[s] (E2 not used). Contrapositive: no size-N(log N)^{k'} circuit family for decision MCSP[(log N)^c] implies none for search-MCSP at size N(log N)^k. This is the direction the H1 transfer needs.

statement:
statement: For any De Morgan formula with L input-variable leaf occurrences, under a restriction in which each input variable is left live with marginal probability p, the expected number of live input-variable leaf occurrences is pL. Repeated occurrences of a variable are counted separately.
proof: For each leaf occurrence i, let I_i be 1 when its input variable is left live and 0 otherwise. The number of live input leaves is sum_{i=1}^L I_i. By linearity of expectation, its expectation is sum_i E[I_i] = sum_i p = pL. This uses only the marginal survival probability and therefore also holds under pairwise-independent restrictions.

statement: Let Phi be a De Morgan formula with L input-variable leaf occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences grouped by gate g, with f_g occurrences of g. Under any restriction distribution where each input variable is live with marginal p and each gate g is nonconstant with probability q_g, the expected number of surviving leaf occurrences is pL + sum_g f_g q_g.
proof: For every input-leaf occurrence i, define indicator I_i that its variable remains live. For every gate-leaf occurrence j of gate g, define indicator J_j that g remains nonconstant. The surviving occurrence count is sum_i I_i + sum_g sum_{j=1}^{f_g} J_j. By linearity of expectation its expectation is sum_i p + sum_g sum_j q_g = pL + sum_g f_g q_g. No independence is needed.

statement: For a finite formula with L input-leaf occurrences, let d_v be the number of occurrences of variable v. Under independent restrictions leaving each variable live with probability p, the surviving input-leaf count X satisfies E[X]=pL and Var(X)=p(1-p) sum_v d_v^2. Consequently, if every d_v<=D, Var(X)<=p(1-p)DL.
proof: Write X=sum_v d_v I_v, where I_v is the Bernoulli-p indicator that v remains live. Then E[X]=sum_v d_v p=pL. Independence gives Var(X)=sum_v d_v^2 Var(I_v)=p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2. Since d_v^2<=D d_v, summing gives sum_v d_v^2<=DL and the stated bound.

label: S0006
statement:
statement: Let F be a finite CNF on n Boolean variables, with clauses indexed by a finite set C. For each clause C_i, let A_i be the set of assignments falsifying C_i. For S subseteq C, let N(S)=|intersection_{i in S} A_i|, with N(empty)=2^n. Then #F = sum_{S subseteq C} (-1)^|S| N(S). If each clause is a disjunction of literals, then N(S)=2^(n-|V(S)|) when the falsification requirements of all clauses in S are consistent, and N(S)=0 otherwise; here V(S) is the set of variables appearing in clauses of S.
proof: An assignment x satisfies F exactly when it lies in none of the events A_i. For each assignment x, the indicator that x lies in none of the A_i equals product_{i in C}(1-1_{A_i}(x)). Expanding the finite product gives sum_{S subseteq C}(-1)^|S| 1_{intersection_{i in S} A_i}(x). Sum over all 2^n assignments and interchange the two finite sums to obtain #F=sum_{S subseteq C}(-1)^|S|N(S). For the stated clause formula, falsifying each literal fixes its variable to one Boolean value. If two such requirements conflict on a variable then the intersection is empty. Otherwise each variable in V(S) is fixed uniquely and every variable outside V(S) is free, so the intersection has exactly 2^(n-|V(S)|) assignments. This includes S=empty by convention.

label: S0007
statement:
statement: Let Phi be a finite De Morgan formula whose leaves are input-variable occurrences and gate occurrences. Under a restriction, suppose each input leaf is retained with probability p and each occurrence of gate type g is retained as nonconstant with probability q_g. Let X be the number of retained leaf occurrences before simplification, and let size(Phi|rho) count leaves after restriction followed by constant folding only. If constant folding does not increase leaf count, then E[size(Phi|rho)] <= pL + sum_g f_g q_g, where L is the number of input leaves and f_g the number of occurrences of type g. Consequently, for every t>0, Pr(size(Phi|rho)>=t) <= (pL+sum_g f_g q_g)/t.
proof: Express X as the sum of indicator variables, one for each leaf occurrence. The input indicators have expectation p and each gate occurrence of type g has expectation q_g. Linearity of expectation gives E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g, with no independence assumption. By the stated constant-folding hypothesis, size(Phi|rho)<=X pointwise, so E[size(Phi|rho)]<=E[X]. Since the residual size is nonnegative, Markov's inequality gives the tail bound.

statement: Let Phi be a binary De Morgan formula with L input-leaf occurrences, each variable appearing at most once. Independently leave each variable live with probability p in [0,1], substitute constants for the other variables, and simplify constant and identity gates. label: S0009
statement:
statement: Let T be any finite rooted full binary tree with at least one leaf, and let X be its number of leaves. If size(T) counts leaves plus internal vertices, then size(T)=2X-1. Consequently, if a restriction/simplification procedure returns either a constant of size 1 or a nonconstant full binary formula R, and X is defined as the number of leaves of R (not the pre-simplification surviving-leaf count), then size(R)=1 when R is constant and size(R)=2X-1 when R is nonconstant.
proof: Let I be the number of internal vertices. Every internal vertex has exactly two children, so the number of edges is 2I. Every finite tree with I+X vertices has I+X-1 edges. Hence 2I=I+X-1, giving I=X-1 and size(T)=I+X=2X-1. The constant case follows from the stipulated size convention.

label: S0010
statement: statement: Residual-leaf charging lemma. Let Phi be a finite binary De Morgan formula tree whose leaves are input-variable occurrences and designated gate-leaf occurrences. Apply a restriction rho, substitute constants at leaves whose predicates become constant, and simplify recursively by the identities AND(0,F)=0, AND(1,F)=F, OR(1,F)=1, OR(0,F)=F. Let L be the number of input-variable leaf occurrences, and let f_g be the number of occurrences of designated gate g. If each input variable occurrence is live with marginal probability p, and each occurrence of g remains nonconstant with probability q_g, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= p L + sum_g f_g q_g, where L(Phi|rho) is the number of leaves in the simplified residual tree. Proof: Before simplification, mark each original leaf occurrence that is still nonconstant after substitution. Every leaf of the simplified tree is an original marked leaf: constant propagation deletes subtrees or replaces a parent by one child, and never creates or duplicates a leaf. Thus pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= X(rho), where X is the number of marked original leaves. By linearity of expectation, E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g; no independence is needed. Taking expectations proves the bound. The exponent-two proposal is false for Phi=x with p=N^{-a}, L=1 and no gate leaves, since its left side is p while its right side is N^{o(1)}p^2=o(p). This lemma repairs it for the exact residual-tree size, though it does not yield P2's desired shrinkage.

label: S0011
statement: statement: Let Phi be a finite formula whose leaves are occurrences indexed by k in a finite set K. Under a random restriction, let I_k be the indicator that occurrence k remains a leaf before constant folding, and set r_k=Pr[I_k=1]. Suppose the residual-size convention counts leaves after constant folding and that this folding never increases the leaf count. Then E[|Phi|_res] <= sum_{k in K} r_k, and for every t>0, Pr(|Phi|_res >= t) <= (sum_{k in K} r_k)/t. Proof: pointwise, |Phi|_res <= sum_k I_k by the nonincrease assumption. label: S0012
statement: statement: Let N>1, let L be the number of input-variable leaf occurrences of a De Morgan formula, and let p=p(N) satisfy p(N)=N^{-epsilon(N)} for some epsilon(N)->0. Under any restriction distribution in which each input variable is live with marginal probability p, the expected number of surviving input-variable leaf occurrences is at most N^{epsilon(N)} p^2 L. Proof: For each occurrence i let I_i be its survival indicator and X=sum_i I_i. By linearity E[X]=pL. Since p=N^{-epsilon(N)}, pL=N^{epsilon(N)}p^2L exactly. No independence assumption is needed. Thus, on the restricted regime p=N^{-o(1)}, the input-leaf contribution to P2' is absorbed by its proposed p^2L term with an explicit subpolynomial factor; this does not control gate-leaf contributions or prove P2'.

label: S0013
statement: statement: Let T be a finite rooted binary formula tree whose leaves are partitioned into input-variable occurrences and gate occurrences. Under a restriction, each input occurrence survives as a variable with marginal probability p, and each occurrence of gate g remains nonconstant with marginal probability q_g. Define the residual tree by replacing every non-surviving leaf by a Boolean constant, evaluating constant subtrees, and suppressing unary internal nodes without duplicating subtrees; count one node for a constant. If T has L input leaves and f_g occurrences of g, then E[size(T|rho)] <= 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g)+1. Proof: Let X count the surviving nonconstant leaves. Indicator variables and linearity of expectation give E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g. If X=0, the residual is a constant of size one. If X>0, any subtree with no surviving nonconstant leaf evaluates to a constant and is collapsed, so every residual leaf descends from one of the X surviving leaves. The residual tree therefore has at most X leaves. A binary tree with t leaves has t-1 internal nodes, hence size at most 2X-1 when X>0. In either case size <=2X+1; taking expectations proves the claim. This repairs the squared-probability target to a linear-probability bound under the stated semantics; it does not establish compatibility with the dossier's intended size measure.

label: S0014
statement: statement: Let T be a finite De Morgan formula tree over literals and constants, with input-variable leaf occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences. Fix a restriction and mark as active each input occurrence whose variable remains live and each gate occurrence whose restricted gate is nonconstant; let X be the number of active occurrences. Simplify T recursively using De Morgan gates: evaluate constant gates, use x AND 1=x, x AND 0=0, x OR 0=x, x OR 1=1 and their dual/complement forms, and suppress unary nodes; never duplicate a subtree. Then the resulting formula has at most X nonconstant leaves, and its node count is at most 2X+1. Consequently, for random restrictions with marginal live probability p on each input variable occurrence and marginal nonconstant probability q_g on each occurrence of gate g, E[size(T|rho)] <= 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g)+1. Proof: By recursive simplification, every residual subtree either is constant or computes a nonconstant function that depends on at least one active leaf below it. In a residual tree that is not constant, every leaf is nonconstant: a constant child of an AND/OR gate either makes the parent constant or is removed by the neutral-element rule, and the same holds for complemented De Morgan forms. Hence every residual leaf is descended from an active occurrence, so the residual has at most X leaves. A binary tree with t leaves has t-1 internal nodes, giving at most 2X-1 nodes when nonconstant; if constant, it has one node. Thus size <=2X+1. Indicator linearity gives E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g, proving the expectation bound. This conclusion depends on full constant/neutral-element simplification; the weaker rule in S0013 that only evaluates constant subtrees is insufficient (e.g. (x AND 1) AND 1 can retain two constant leaves when x is active).

statement:
statement: Let Phi be a finite formula whose residual size after restriction is defined syntactically, before Boolean simplification, by counting each surviving input-variable leaf occurrence once and replacing every non-surviving input leaf by a constant. If Phi has L input-variable leaf occurrences and each underlying variable is live with marginal probability p, then E[L(Phi|rho)] = pL. Consequently, for Phi=x, p=N^{-alpha} with any fixed alpha>0, and any prefactor a(N)=N^{o(1)}, the bound E[L(Phi|rho)] <= a(N)p^2 L fails for all sufficiently large N.
proof: For each leaf occurrence i, define I_i(rho)=1 when its variable is live and 0 otherwise. By the stipulated syntactic size convention, L(Phi|rho)=sum_{i=1}^L I_i(rho). Therefore linearity of expectation gives E[L(Phi|rho)]=sum_i E[I_i]=pL; no independence is needed. For Phi=x, L=1 and p=N^{-alpha}, so the proposed right side is a(N)N^{-2alpha}, whereas the left side is N^{-alpha}. Since a(N)=N^{o(1)}, the ratio of left to right is N^{alpha-o(1)}, which tends to infinity; thus the inequality fails eventually. The single-variable restriction distribution is pairwise independent vacuously.
scope: Syntactic residual leaf count before Boolean simplification; any finite formula for the equality, and the single-leaf formula for the asymptotic counterexample. This does not address residual size after Boolean simplification.

statement: For a binary De Morgan formula with L variable-leaf occurrences, let X be the number left live by a restriction. Substitute constants, then recursively eliminate every AND/OR gate with a constant child by its Boolean identity. The residual node count is at most 2X+1. If each variable is live with marginal p, its expected node count is at most 2pL+1.
proof: The simplification duplicates no subtree. If the output is constant, size is 1. Otherwise every leaf is a live variable and every internal node has two children. If there are X' leaves, then X'<=X and a finite full binary tree has X'-1 internal nodes; total size is 2X'-1<=2X+1. Also X is the sum of L occurrence indicators of mean p, so E[X]=pL by linearity. Taking expectations proves the expectation bound.

label: S0017
statement: statement: Let T be a finite binary De Morgan formula tree whose leaves consist of ordinary input-variable occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences. Under any restriction, suppose each leaf occurrence is either replaced by a Boolean constant or remains as one nonconstant leaf, and simplification repeatedly deletes a constant child using the Boolean identities for AND and OR, without expanding or duplicating any surviving leaf. Let X be the number of surviving leaf occurrences. Then the simplified residual has at most 2X+1 nodes. If input leaf i survives with probability p_i and gate leaf j survives with probability q_j, its expected node count is at most 2(sum_i p_i + sum_j q_j)+1. Proof: the simplification preserves the binary-tree property and never duplicates leaves. If the output is constant, it has one node. Otherwise all remaining leaves are among the X surviving occurrences, so their number X' is at most X. In any finite full binary tree with X' leaves, the number of internal nodes is X'-1, hence total nodes are 2X'-1 <= 2X+1. Taking expectations and applying linearity to X gives E[X]=sum_i p_i+sum_j q_j, without any independence assumption; therefore E[nodes] <= 2E[X]+1. Scope is only the stated constant-simplification model and total node count.

Note that a gate g=(x,x) gives x fan-out 2, so it is excluded from K=0.

label: S0028
statement: LEMMA (repair of V3; CLAIMED). Setting: fan-in-2 DAG circuit with output out; G = reachable gates, S = |G|; a path is a sequence of child slots from out; N(v) = number of such paths ending at v; fo(w) = number of child slots pointing at w from reachable gates (with multiplicity); L = number of input leaves of the formula unfolding = sum over inputs x of N(x). (a) L = 1 + sum_{g in G} N(g). Proof: each reachable v != out satisfies N(v) = sum over its parent slots of N(parent); summing over v != out gives sum_inputs N + sum_{G, g != out} N(g) = 2 sum_G N(g); hence sum_inputs N = sum_G N(g) + N(out) = 1 + sum_G N(g), since N(out) = 1. (b) N(v) <= prod_{w reachable, fo(w) >= 2} fo(w). Proof: map each path P to the vector of slot indices it takes at reused nodes it visits (default index 1 when not visited). Two distinct paths to v agree up to a first node w where they take different slots (a prefix cannot end at the same v in a DAG), and both visit w, so the map is injective. (c) Hence L <= 1 + S * prod fo(w) <= 1 + S * 2^R. When all reused fo <= 2, L <= 1 + S * 2^K. Checks: the chain c_i = (c_{i-1}, c_{i-1}) has S=K, L=2^K <= 1+K*2^K; the f5 counterexample has L=15 <= 1+6*16=97 (weak but valid); 0 violations of 1+S*2^K when fo<=2 in cm-6ef7658c8ac24a87. Gap that remains: the 2^K factor is exponential in K, so this helps the R-MCSP route only if K = O(log S) or after a reduction that removes functional redundancy. Barrier labels: not applicable (purely combinatorial on circuits, no oracle or natural-property claim).

statement: REPAIR OF S0020 (conditional on the child bound). Let g = (ta, tb) be a fan-in-2 gate whose reachable gate sets reach_gates(ta) and reach_gates(tb) are disjoint. Let S = number of reachable gates, K = number of reachable nodes (inputs or gates) with fan-out >= 2 within the reachable part, L = leaf count of the formula unfolding. Assume L_a <= 2^{K_a}(S_a+1) and L_b <= 2^{K_b}(S_b+1). Then L_g <= 2^{K_g}(S_g+1). Proof: (1) S_g = S_a + S_b + 1 by gate-disjointness. (2) K_g >= max(K_a, K_b): reach(ta), reach(tb) are subsets of reach(g) and fan-outs computed inside reach(g) are at least those computed inside the child reach sets. (3) L_g = L_a + L_b since the unfolding of g is the tree of g. (4) With K* = max(K_a, K_b): L_g <= 2^{K*}(S_a+S_b+2) = 2^{K*}(S_g+1) <= 2^{K_g}(S_g+1). The equality K_g = K_a + K_b is not used.

label: S0032
statement: LEMMA (repair of S0028 part (b); CLAIMED pending review). Setting as in S0028: DAG with fan-in 2, out = output, G = reachable gates, S = |G|, fo(w) = number of child slots from reachable gates pointing at w, R = {w reachable : fo(w) >= 2}, A(v) = strict ancestors of v (nodes w != v with a path from w to v through out-direction edges), N(v) = number of paths from out to v counted with slot multiplicity. Claim: N(v) <= product of fo(w) over w in R with w in A(v) union {v}. Proof by induction over the topological order from out. Base: N(out) = 1 and fo(out) = 0, so the product is 1. Step: for v != out with parent slots of parents p_i of multiplicity m_i, sum of m_i = fo(v) = k, and N(v) = sum m_i N(p_i). Let Q = product of fo(w) over w in R intersect A(v). For each parent p_i, A(p_i) union {p_i} is contained in A(v), so by induction N(p_i) <= Q. If k >= 2, then v is in R and N(v) <= sum m_i Q = k Q = fo(v) Q, which is the bound for v. If k = 1, then v is not in R and N(v) = N(p) <= Q, which is the bound for v. Consequence: L = 1 + sum over g in G of N(g) (identity from summing slot counts over all reachable non-output nodes), so L <= 1 + S * prod over R of fo(w) <= 1 + S * 2^{sum over R of (fo(w) - 1)}. Scope: general fan-in-2 DAG unfolding; no oracle, no natural-property claim. Limits: (i) the factor 2^r is exponential in r, so this does NOT meet the polynomial-in-r shape (C S (r+1)^c, c < 1) of R-MCSP unless r = O(1) after a reduction; (ii) the chain c_i = (c_{i-1}, c_{i-1}) has S = K, L = 2^K, so an exponential factor in the reuse count is unavoidable for naive unfoldings; the open point is a reduction to functionally minimal circuits. Finite check: code run result to be recorded.

statement: LEMMA (matrix core of the T1 Hadamard lemma, S-c04b3d909c): for any field F (in particular GF(p)) and any a x b matrices A, B over F, rank(A o B) <= rank(A) * rank(B), where o is the entrywise product. Proof: write A = U V^T with U a x rA, V b x rA (rank factorisation), and B = X Y^T with X a x rB, Y b x rB. Then (A o B)_{ij} = sum_{k,l} (U_{ik} X_{il}) (V_{jk} Y_{jl}), so A o B = sum_{k,l} (U_k o X_l)(V_k o Y_l)^T, a sum of rA*rB rank-one matrices. Consequence: for functions f, g: {0,1}^n -> F with cut matrices M_i(f), M_i(g), the cut matrix of f*g is M_i(f) o M_i(g), so cut rank(fg) <= cut rank(f) * cut rank(g). Scope: all fields, all dimensions. Note: this is a classical Schur-product rank inequality; the record is a reproduction and a bookkeeping step, not progress on P vs NP.

statement: CLAIMED (proof attempt, not reviewed) LEMMA S-6ce27138d2, two-sweep form. Setting: field GF(p); cores G_k[b] of size r_{k-1} x r_k (b in {0,1}), r_0 = r_n = 1, f(x) = G_1[x_1]...G_n[x_n] nonzero; M_k(f) = 2^k x 2^(n-k) cut matrix; c_k = rank M_k(f). Statement: after one L->R sweep (step k: rref U_k of the unfolding U with rows (a,b) = G_k[b][a], U_k = B_k R_k, set G_k[b] := rows of B_k, G_{k+1}[b] := R_k G_{k+1}[b]) and one R->L sweep (mirror image), the bond dims equal c_k for 1<=k<=n-1 and f is unchanged. Proof: (i) Each elimination step preserves f: new G_k[b] R_k G_{k+1} = U_b G_{k+1} = G_k[b] G_{k+1} because U = B R. (ii) Invariant after the L->R sweep: the prefix matrix P_k(x_1..x_k) = G_1[x_1]...G_k[x_k] (2^k x s_k) has full column rank s_k, by induction (the pivot columns of U_k are independent, so B_k has full column rank, and P_{k-1} full column rank is preserved under the map induced by B_k). Hence M_k(f) = P_k S_k gives rank M_k = rank S_k <= s_k. (iii) The R->L sweep at bond k is the mirror image of step (i), so it fixes the new bond dim as the rank of the current suffix matrix; this rank equals c_k because the L->R invariant (ii) makes the suffix rank equal the cut rank. (iv) Full column rank of the prefix (ii) is restored at bond k after step k+1 of the R->L sweep, since that step only multiplies core k by an r_k x s'_k matrix whose columns are independent (pivot columns), so P_k A keeps full column rank s'_k = c_k. Hence bond k dimension = c_k.

statement: PROOF of Lemma A. (1) Fredholm over GF(2): Ax=b is solvable iff there is no lambda with lambda^T A=0 and lambda^T b=1. Such a lambda is supported on S and gives sum_{i in S} lambda_i v_i = e. So S is inconsistent iff e in span(v_S). (2) Minimal inconsistent S gives a circuit C=S+e: (i) S is independent, since a nonempty R in S with sum_R v_i=0 and r in R gives v_r in span(v_{S-r}), so S-r is inconsistent, contradicting minimality. (ii) e in span(S) and S independent make C=S+e dependent. (iii) A proper subset of C is either a subset of S (independent by (i)) or U+e with U a proper subset of S. The latter is dependent iff e in span(v_U) iff U inconsistent, impossible since U is consistent by minimality. So C is a circuit containing e. (3) Conversely, let C be a circuit containing e and S=C-e. C is minimal dependent, so v_S is independent and e in span(v_S), hence S is inconsistent. If S-i were inconsistent for some i in S, then e in span(v_{S-i}) would give a dependency inside C-i, contradicting minimality of C. So S is minimal. The two directions are inverse. QED. Consequence: the affine clutter is a binary-matroid port, and the port-level elimination axiom 'for A,B in cl and f in A&B there is D in cl with D inside (A u B)-f' is NOT implied by this. Hand counterexample (binary, graphic): a multigraph with vertices x,u,v,y, edges a,c parallel between x and u, edge e=(u,v), edges b,d parallel-in-role between v and y, edge f=(y,x). The circuits C1={a,e,b,f} and C2={c,e,d,f} give A=C1-e and B=C2-e with A&B={f}, and the only cycles in (A u B) minus f avoid e, so no member of the port lies inside (A u B)-f.

structure.lemma: Lemma A (affine clutter = port). Let c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], a_i in GF(2)^n, b_i in GF(2), denoting the equation a_i.x=b_i. Put v_i=(a_i,b_i) in GF(2)^(n+1), e=(0,...,0,1), and let M be the binary matroid on {v_1..v_m,e}. Then the family of minimal inconsistent subsets S of [m] equals {C minus e : C a circuit of M with e in C}. So the minimal-UNSAT clutter of any affine system is the port of M at e. Every binary matroid with a non-loop element e arises this way (linear change of basis sends e to the last unit vector).

label: S0006
statement: For all matrices A,B over GF(2) and vectors c, the projection R={x: exists y, Ax+By=c} is affine. Proof: Let L={lambda: lambda^T B=0}. By finite-dimensional linear algebra, z is in im(B) iff lambda^T z=0 for every lambda in the left nullspace L. Thus x is in R iff c-Ax is in im(B), iff lambda^T A x=lambda^T c for every lambda in L. This is an intersection of affine hyperplanes, hence affine (possibly empty).

label: S0005
statement: LEMMA (single gate, any field). Let f(x)=[w.x >= t] with integer weights, W = max_i |w_i|, and let [n] = S disjoint-union T with S, T nonempty. Let M be the 2^|S| x 2^|T| cut matrix M[a,b] = f(a,b). Then for every field F, rank_F(M) = number of distinct NONZERO rows of M, and this number is at most min(2^|S|, 2W|T|+2). Proof: row a is the indicator of R_a = {b : w_T.b >= t - w_S.a}; these supports are nested (threshold sets of one linear form). Order the distinct nonzero supports R_1 strictly-in R_2 ... strictly-in R_d and pick b_i in R_i minus R_{i-1} (R_0 empty). Then M[row R_j, col b_i] = [j >= i], unitriangular, so rank >= d; rank <= d is trivial. Bound: w_T.b lies in an integer set of size at most 2W|T|+1; nonempty threshold sets are determined by their least value, so d <= 2W|T|+1 <= 2W|T|+2. The earlier draft said 'rank = number of distinct rows' and omitted the nonzero restriction; that version is false when an all-zero row occurs (example w=(1), t=5, n=2, S={x1}: rank 0, one distinct row).

statement:
statement: Coefficient bound for rank-r threshold evaluation. Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix of rank r>=1 with |W_ji|<=B, where B>=1. Choose r linearly independent rows M and r columns J such that M_J is nonsingular. For every row w_j of W, write w_j=a_j M over Q and put D=|det(M_J)|. Then D a_j is an integer vector and every coordinate has absolute value at most r r! B^r. Consequently, for any rational threshold t_j, the comparison w_j·x >= t_j for x in {0,1}^n is exactly equivalent to (D a_j)·(Mx) >= D t_j, and the latter can be evaluated with bit complexity polynomial in r, log(B+1), and the binary encoding length of t_j.
proof: Since the rows of M are independent and w_j is in their span, there is a unique a_j with w_j=a_jM. Restricting to columns J gives w_j[J]=a_j M_J, hence a_j=w_j[J]M_J^{-1}. Write q=det(M_J), so M_J^{-1}=adj(M_J)/q. Therefore D a_j=|q|w_j[J]adj(M_J)/q=sgn(q)w_j[J]adj(M_J), an integer vector. Each coordinate is a sum of r terms, each a product of one entry of w_j[J], bounded by B, and one (r-1)-by-(r-1) determinant of M_J, whose permutation expansion has at most (r-1)! terms each of magnitude at most B^(r-1). Thus each coordinate is at most r B (r-1)! B^(r-1)=r! B^r; the stated looser bound r r! B^r follows. Also D>0, so multiplying the inequality w_j·x>=t_j by D preserves its direction; w_j·x=a_j·(Mx), giving the claimed equivalence. Each coefficient D a_j has O(r log(r+1)+r log(B+1)) bits, each coordinate of Mx has O(log(nB+1)) bits, and exact rational comparison with Dt_j can be done using integers whose bit lengths are polynomial in these quantities and the input encoding length of t_j.
evidence: General determinant and adjugate argument above. Finite corroboration only: independent histogram-vs-brute-force verification cm-680af5c7f0c142f7 checked 22,506 generated cases; it does not prove the general lemma or an asymptotic speedup.

statement: Lattice-coordinate exact DP. Let M be an integer r-by-n matrix of rank r, and let H be an integer basis matrix for its column lattice L=M Z^n, so H is nonsingular and every column M_i equals H g_i for a unique g_i in Z^r. For each coordinate k set A_k=sum_{i=1}^n |(g_i)_k|. For any Boolean function F determined by threshold comparisons of rows W_j=a_j M with rational thresholds t_j, the number of x in {0,1}^n with F(x)=1 is computed exactly by a DP over z=sum_i g_i x_i, evaluating F from Mx=Hz. The DP visits at most product_{k=1}^r(2A_k+1) states and uses O(n times that bound) additions, plus polynomial bit complexity per operation.
proof: Initialize N_0(0)=1 and all other counts zero. For i=1,...,n update N_i(z)=N_{i-1}(z)+N_{i-1}(z-g_i), treating absent states as zero. Inductively, N_i(z) counts exactly the prefixes (x_1,...,x_i) with sum_{h<=i}g_h x_h=z: the two terms partition prefixes by x_i=0 or 1. Every coordinate z_k lies in [-A_k,A_k], so there are at most product_k(2A_k+1) possible states at each layer. At the final layer Mx=H sum_i g_i x_i=Hz; therefore every original threshold comparison, and hence F(x), is determined exactly by z. Summing N_n(z) over accepting z gives the desired count. Counts have at most n+1 bits; state coordinates and exact rational threshold comparisons have bit complexity polynomial in the input bit lengths and n.
evidence: Exact recurrence and state-range proof above. No finite computation is claimed.

label: S0004
statement:
statement: Magnitude-independent DP for repeated scaled coordinate columns. Let r,t,q be positive integers and let M be the r-by-rt integer matrix whose columns consist of t copies of q e_k for each k in {1,...,r}, in any fixed order. For every function F:{0,...,qt}^r->{0,1}, the number of x in {0,1}^{rt} with F(Mx)=1 is computable exactly by a layered DP using at most (t+1)^r states per layer and O(rt(t+1)^r) integer additions. The state count is independent of q; arithmetic bit lengths are O(rt+log q). Here rank(M)=r and n=rt, so the result includes rank proportional to n when t is a fixed positive integer.
proof: Write column i as q g_i, where each g_i is some standard basis vector e_k and each e_k occurs exactly t times. Run the recurrence N_0(0)=1 and N_i(z)=N_{i-1}(z)+N_{i-1}(z-g_i), with absent states zero. Induction on i shows N_i(z) counts exactly the prefixes whose sum of g-columns equals z. At every layer, each coordinate z_k is an integer between 0 and the number of e_k columns processed, hence between 0 and t; therefore at most (t+1)^r states occur. At the final layer Mx=qz, so F(Mx)=F(qz) is determined by z and summing N_{rt}(z) over accepting z gives the exact count. Each count is at most 2^{rt}, requiring at most rt+1 bits; coordinates require O(log(t+1)) bits and computing qz requires O(log q+log(t+1)) bits per coordinate. Each transition uses a constant number of additions, proving the stated operation count and bit-size bound.
evidence: Exact recurrence, induction, and coordinate-range argument in the proof. No finite computation is claimed.

statement: Magnitude-independent DP with explicit evaluator cost. Let r,t,q be positive integers and M an r-by-rt integer matrix containing exactly t copies of each column q e_k (k=1,...,r). Let F:{0,q,...,qt}^r->{0,1} be supplied by an evaluator that, on any argument in this domain, uses at most T_F bit operations. Then # {x in {0,1}^{rt}: F(Mx)=1} can be computed exactly using at most O(rt(t+1)^r) integer additions and (t+1)^r evaluations of F, with all integers having O(rt+log(qt)) bits. statement: Let p in {2,3}, S,N >= 1, H a matrix over F_p with S rows and N columns. If N > (p-1)S, there is a nonzero k in {0,1}^N with Hk = 0 over F_p. Consequence (R1): let C_m be a LINEAR staged realization over F_p of total exact Search-MCSP^A[s] (state q_0=0, q_{t+1}=M_t q_t + z_t v_t over F_p with z_t in {0,1}, decoder D an arbitrary function of q_N). Then S(C_m) >= N/(p-1) = 2^m/(p-1). For p=3: S(C_m) >= 2^(m-1). The bound is tight for the kernel argument: for p=3 the 2S columns e_1,e_1,...,e_S,e_S admit no nonzero Boolean kernel vector.
derivation: (1) q_N = H f is linear in the input bit-vector f in {0,1}^N, with H in F_p^{S x N} (column t = (product of M after step t) v_t). (2) Chevalley-Warning: take the S polynomials g_i(x) = sum_t H[i,t] x_t^(p-1) over F_p in N variables. Each has degree p-1, total degree S(p-1) < N. The number of common zeros in F_p^N is divisible by p. x=0 is a zero, so the count is at least p >= 2, hence there is a zero x != 0. (3) k_t := x_t^(p-1) is in {0,1} and is nonzero (since x != 0), and sum_t H[i,t] k_t = g_i(x) = 0, i.e. Hk = 0. (4) Totality: f=0 is in Im_s (constant table has a size-1 circuit), so D(q_N(0)) = D(0) must be a circuit computing 0. Since q_N(k) = q_N(0), D(k) equals the same circuit C. If k is in Im_s, the correct answer for k is a circuit computing k != 0, contradicting C computing 0 on input 0 and k simultaneously; if k is not in Im_s, the correct answer is 'none', contradicting D(0) being a circuit. So no nonzero Boolean kernel vector exists, forcing N <= (p-1)S. (5) N = 2^m gives S >= 2^(m-1). Contradiction with S <= s(m)^c needs log s(m) = o(m), e.g. s polynomial. The Gamma clause is not used. Scope: linear updates (M_t, v_t fixed over F_p, z_t Boolean) and any decoder with access only to q_N; oracle gates allowed only in the decoder. Oracle gates in updates break step (1).

structure.evidence: Independent exhaustive check cm-2b6f7b3c858a4c26 (own code, different method from the Chevalley-Warning proof): max length of a zero-subsum-free sequence in F_3^S is 2,4,6 for S=1,2,3 and in F_2^S is 1,2,3,4 for S=1..4, matching S(p-1) exactly. Failure it could catch: an off-by-one in the subsequence convention or a wrong Davenport constant (the alternative 'max = S' for p=3 is excluded at S=2: 4 vs 2).

label: S0006
statement: LEMMA (search-version repair of S0001 step 4; claimed by R1674 claude-haiku-5-5, CLAIMED until reviewed by another model family). SETTING: p in {2,3}, N,S >= 1. A linear staged realization over F_p: state q_0 = 0, q_{t+1} = M_t q_t + z_t v_t with M_t in F_p^{S x S}, v_t in F_p^S fixed and independent of the input; input z = the truth table, z in {0,1}^N, N = 2^m; decoder D maps the final state q_N in F_p^S to a circuit or to 'none'. REQUIRED: if z has a circuit of size <= s then D(q_N(z)) is a circuit computing z; otherwise D(q_N(z)) = none. CLAIM: N <= (p-1)S, hence S >= 2^m/(p-1). PROOF: (1) q_N(z) = H z with H in F_p^{S x N}, column t = (M_N...M_{t+1}) v_t. (2) Suppose N > (p-1)S. The S polynomials g_i(x) = sum_t H[i,t] x_t^{p-1} have degree p-1 in N variables, total degree S(p-1) < N. By Chevalley-Warning the number of common zeros in F_p^N is divisible by p; x = 0 is a zero, so there is a zero x != 0. (3) k_t := x_t^{p-1} lies in {0,1}, k != 0, and Hk = 0, so q_N(k) = q_N(0) =: q. (4) Let C = D(q). Input 0^N has a size-1 circuit, so C computes 0 (C != 'none'). Case A: k has a circuit of size <= s. Then D(q) must compute k != 0, but C computes 0. Contradiction. Case B: k has no such circuit. Then D(q) must be 'none', but D(q) = C is a circuit. Contradiction. Both cases contradict, so no nonzero Boolean kernel vector exists, which forces N <= (p-1)S. NOTE: this does NOT use any yes-instance condition on k, so it closes the decoder gap G0004 for the SEARCH problem (the decision version still needs D(k) = 0, which is not provided). EVIDENCE: arithmetic core of Chevalley-Warning step, cm-f22a479a94be4e3c and cm-69ddc45df9024ade (0 counterexamples). Finite check of the kernel fact, cm-e7305048fc394206 (N=4): p2_S3 0 trivial-kernel H (predicted 0), p2_S4 20160 (predicted >0), p3_S1 0 (predicted 0), p3_S2 720 (predicted >0). All four matched the prediction; this checks the Davenport-type threshold at N=4 only, not the decoder argument. SCOPE: linear input-independent updates over F_p; S counts F_p coordinates (bit size is S log p); decoder sees only q_N; oracle gates allowed only in D. Nonlinear update gates are NOT covered, so this is a restricted-model bound, not progress on P vs NP by itself. CONSEQUENCE: for s(m) = poly(m), S >= 2^m/(p-1) exceeds any poly(s) bound, so no linear staged realization of this size exists.

label: S0012
statement:
LEMMA (Kernel counting closes collision step for linear F_2 realizations):

Let a linear F_2 staged realization (input-independent updates M_t ∈ F_2^{S×S}, v_t ∈ F_2^S, decoder D: F_2^S → {0,1}) compute the search-MCSP decision function D(x) = [x has circuit size ≤ s] on N = 2^n-bit inputs, with exact totality.

Define the cumulative column matrix C = [M_N...M_1 v_1 | ... | M_N...M_t v_t | ... | v_N] ∈ F_2^{S×N}. The final state on input z ∈ F_2^N is q(z) = C z + q_0 (q_0 fixed). The kernel K = {z : C z = 0} has size |K| = 2^{N - rank(C)} ≥ 2^{N - S}.

The set of yes-instances Y_s = {x : circuit size(x) ≤ s} satisfies |Y_s| ≤ ∑_{i=1}^s (number of circuits of size i) ≤ ∑_{i=1}^s (c i)^i ≤ s (c s)^s = 2^{O(s log s)} for some constant c.

If N - S > O(s log s) + 1, then |K| > |Y_s| + 1, so there exists nonzero k ∈ K with k ∉ Y_s (i.e., D(k) = 0). Since 0 ∈ Y_s (constant table has O(1) circuit), we have D(0) = 1 ≠ 0 = D(k). But q(0) = q_0 = q(k), so the decoder outputs the same bit on both inputs, contradiction.

Therefore any linear F_2 realization computing search-MCSP must satisfy N ≤ S + O(s log s).

For s(n) = 2^{n/log* n}, N = 2^n, this gives S ≥ 2^n - O(2^{n/log* n} · n/log* n) = 2^n - o(2^n). Hence S = Ω(N), i.e., space must be linear in input length.

This closes the quantifier gap in G0004 by exhibiting a specific no-instance k (via counting, not by construction) that must exist in the kernel whenever the space bound is sublinear.

Assumptions verified:
(i) Decoder depends only on final state (by definition of staged realization)
(ii) M_t, v_t input-independent (by definition)
(iii) Totality gives exact computation of D on all inputs (search-MCSP hypothesis)
(iv) 0 ∈ Y_s always (constant-0 table has circuit size O(1) ≤ s for all s ≥ 1)

This lemma is RESTRICTED to linear F_2 updates (R1 class). It does not apply to affine (shifted) updates or nonlinear gates.

label: S0014
statement: CLAIMED L-lin (R1, F_2-linear input-independent streaming with final-state decoder). Let N=2^m, D_s = indicator of circuit size <= s over the full binary basis, P_s = {k in F_2^N : D_s(x xor k)=D_s(x) for all x}. Any realization with state Mx+c (M in F_2^{S x N}) computing D_s on all N-bit inputs has S >= N - d_s, where d_s = dim P_s <= log2(m+s) + s*log2(16(m+s)^2). Proof: (1) ker M is contained in P_s, since state(x xor k)=state(x) when Mk=0 and the decoder reads only the state; (2) rank M >= N - dim ker M >= N - d_s and rank M <= S; (3) P_s is a subgroup containing 0, and D_s^{-1}(1) is a union of its cosets, so |P_s| <= |D_s^{-1}(1)| <= (m+s)(16(m+s)^2)^s by counting circuits.

structure.evidence: cm-2d4d91349bc541bc (EXPLORATORY): m=3, d_s=1 for s=1,2,3 (exact up to 3 gates), parity control dim 7. The computation checks only the small case; the general lemma is proved by hand above. Not reviewed (same model family as claimant).
structure.gap: Restricted to F_2-linear input-independent realizations. Does not close G0001 (oracle-free uniform machines, nonlinear updates). Cross-family review of steps (1)-(3) needed before SURVIVED_REVIEW. Bound is vacuous at m=3 and strong only when 2^m >> poly(s).

label: S0016
statement: L-lin-exact (R1, F_2-affine input-independent realizations, arbitrary decoder of the final state): for N=2^m, D_s the indicator of circuit size <= s, P_s = {k : D_s(x xor k)=D_s(x) for all x}, d_s = dim P_s. (a) Any realization g(Mx+c)=D_s(x) with M in F_2^{S x N} has S >= N - d_s, since ker M is contained in P_s and rank M = N - dim ker M. label: S0017
statement:
step: Let N = 2^m, let Y be a nonempty fixed subset of F_2^N, and let sigma(x) = Mx + c with M in F_2^{S x N}, c in F_2^S. Suppose a decoder D reads only sigma(x), outputs a circuit computing x whenever x is in Y, and outputs none whenever x is not in Y. Then S >= N. Proof: fix x in Y and k in ker M. Then sigma(x+k) = sigma(x), so D(sigma(x+k)) = D(sigma(x)) = C, where C is not none and computes x. Since D outputs none on non-members, x+k is in Y. Then D's answer C must compute x+k as well; since C computes x, we get x+k = x, so k = 0. Hence ker M = {0}, rank M = N, and S >= N. Tightness: M = I, c = 0. Scope: F_2-affine realizations with input-independent linear updates; decoder reads only the final state; none required on non-members; Y nonempty and fixed in advance. Not covered: nonlinear or input-dependent streaming updates, decoders that use update history, and decoders that may answer none on members.
evidence: Hand proof (above), checked for the restricted case. Supporting lab check cm-14e4fda8f7b44289 (exploratory, N=8, random Y of size 38): 0 of 400 maps with S < N were consistent with the none-reporting exact decoder; the identity map was consistent. The random check is supporting only, not a verification of the proof.

label: S0023
statement: LEMMA (restricted, F_2-affine, strict decoder). Fix s >= 1 and N = 2^m. Let Yes_s = {x in F_2^N : x has a circuit of size <= s} and No_s = F_2^N minus Yes_s. Let sigma(x) = b + A x in F_2^S, with b and A fixed and independent of x, and let D: F_2^S -> {circuits} union {none} satisfy: D(sigma(x)) computes x for x in Yes_s, and D(sigma(x)) = none for x in No_s. Then ker A = {0}, hence rank A = N and S >= N. Proof: 0 is in Yes_s (the constant-0 circuit has size 1 <= s). Let k != 0 with Ak = 0. Then sigma(k) = sigma(0) = b, so D outputs the same value O on k and 0, and O is a circuit computing 0 because 0 is in Yes_s. If k is in Yes_s, O must compute k, impossible since k != 0. If k is in No_s, O must be none, contradicting that O is a circuit. Hence ker A = {0}; rank-nullity gives rank A = N, so S >= N.

structure.evidence: Scope: strict (none-reporting) decoder as required by MMW19 (per R1674 approach 2a0f5fddf05248d5); F_2-affine input-independent state only; lenient search is NOT covered (G0005); nonlinear updates and F_p with p=3 are NOT covered, so G0004 stays open in general and closes only for this restricted class. Computation cm-c0bac0de48b5419b (own enumeration, direct over linear maps F_2^4 -> F_2^S, S=1..5): counts {1:0, 2:0, 3:0, 4:20160, 5:624960}, matching the prediction (20160 = |GL(4,2)|; 624960 = 31*30*28*24 injective 4->5 maps). Limits: the YES set is a toy set {0, x1, x2} chosen by me, not the real circuit-size threshold; the code's grouping criterion is the same fiber logic as the lemma, so the run checks the fiber arithmetic on a toy instance, not the claim for Search-MCSP. Author is claude-haiku-5-5, same family as the claimants, so this is NOT a cross-family review. Needs a cross-family reviewer to check the lemma statement (in particular: the strict-decoder assumption, the affine state b + Ax, and whether 'closes G0004' is valid for the restricted class) and to set confirms_closure.

label: S0024
statement:
statement: LEMMA L_dec (decision form of S0014, no decoder-strictness needed). Let N >= 1, h: F_2^N -> {0,1}, and Per(h) = {v in F_2^N : h(x+v) = h(x) for all x}, a subspace. Let A in F_2^{S x N}, b in F_2^S, g: F_2^S -> {0,1} with h(x) = g(b + Ax) for all x. Then S >= rank A >= N - dim Per(h).
proof: Let K = ker A. For k in K and any x: b + A(x+k) = b + Ax, so h(x+k) = g(b+A(x+k)) = g(b+Ax) = h(x). Hence K is contained in Per(h), so dim K <= dim Per(h). Rank-nullity gives rank A = N - dim K >= N - dim Per(h), and rank A <= S. Scope: decision version only. The map g is a decision decoder for h; any decoder that outputs a circuit or none is covered once it is converted to the bit g(y) = [D(y) is a circuit]. statement:
REPAIR of S0014 for SEARCH version (R1, F_2-linear/affine staged realizations). Let N=2^m. The total search problem SearchMCSP^A[s] receives x∈F_2^N and must output a circuit of size ≤s computing x, or 'none' if none exists. Consider a one-pass streaming algorithm with affine state updates over F_2: q_0 = c_0, q_t = M_t q_{t-1} + L_t x_t + c_t for t=1..N, where M_t∈F_2^{S×S}, L_t∈F_2^{S×1}, c_t∈F_2^S. Final state q_N = M x + c with M∈F_2^{S×N}, c∈F_2^S. Decoder D: F_2^S → {circuits of size ≤s} ∪ {'none'}. Correctness: ∀x, if x has circuit size ≤s then D(q_N(x)) is a circuit computing x; else D(q_N(x)) = 'none'.

Claim: S ≥ N.
Proof: The all-zero truth table 0^N has a trivial circuit (constant 0, size O(1) ≤ s), so it is a YES instance. Thus D(q_N(0)) = D(c) = C_0, a circuit computing the constant 0 function.
Now suppose k ∈ ker M, k ≠ 0. Then q_N(k) = M k + c = c = q_N(0). By correctness, D(q_N(k)) = D(c) = C_0. But C_0 computes the constant 0 function. For this to be the correct output on input k, we would need k to be the constant 0 function, i.e., k = 0^N. Contradiction since k ≠ 0. Therefore ker M = {0}. Hence rank M = N. Since M has S rows, S ≥ rank M = N = 2^m.

This bound S ≥ 2^m is exponential in m, while s^O(1) is polynomial in m (since s ≥ m). Therefore no R1 realization can have S = s^O(1), proving equation (8) for the class R1.

statement: LEMMA (R1, F_2-linear input-independent streaming for DECISION-MCSP). Let N=2^m. Let D_s: F_2^N → {0,1} be the indicator of circuit size ≤ s over the full binary basis (with constants as gates of size 1). Let P_s = {k ∈ F_2^N : D_s(x⊕k) = D_s(x) for all x ∈ F_2^N}. Consider a one-pass streaming algorithm with affine state updates over F_2: initial state c ∈ F_2^S, update state ← M·x_t + state for each input bit x_t (M ∈ F_2^{S×N} fixed), final state = Mx + c. A final-state decoder D: F_2^S → {0,1} computes D_s correctly on all inputs: D(Mx+c) = D_s(x) for all x. Then S ≥ N - d_s where d_s = dim(span(P_s)) ≤ log2(m+s) + s·log2(16(m+s)^2).
proof: Proof: (1) For any k ∈ ker(M), we have M(x⊕k)+c = Mx+Mk+c = Mx+c for all x. Thus the final state is identical for x and x⊕k. Since the decoder D reads only the final state, D(M(x⊕k)+c) = D(Mx+c) for all x. By correctness, D_s(x⊕k) = D_s(x) for all x. Hence k ∈ P_s. So ker(M) ⊆ P_s, and dim(ker(M)) ≤ dim(span(P_s)) = d_s. (2) By rank-nullity, rank(M) = N - dim(ker(M)) ≥ N - d_s. Since M has S rows, rank(M) ≤ S. Thus S ≥ N - d_s. (3) P_s is a subgroup of F_2^N (if k1,k2 ∈ P_s then D_s(x⊕k1⊕k2)=D_s(x⊕k1)=D_s(x), so k1⊕k2 ∈ P_s). The set Y = D_s^{-1}(1) (truth tables with circuit size ≤ s) is a union of cosets of P_s: if y ∈ Y and k ∈ P_s, then D_s(y⊕k)=D_s(y)=1, so y⊕k ∈ Y. Hence |P_s| ≤ |Y|. The number of circuits of size ≤ s over the full binary basis with constants is at most (m+s)·(16(m+s)^2)^s (each gate: choose type from {AND,OR,NOT,constant}, choose up to 2 inputs from m+s previous gates/constants). Each circuit computes one function, so |Y| ≤ (m+s)·(16(m+s)^2)^s. Thus d_s = log2|P_s| ≤ log2|Y| ≤ log2(m+s) + s·log2(16(m+s)^2). ∎

statement: LEMMA (bounded-degree final map collision). Let p be prime, N,S >= 1, and d >= 0. Suppose F:F_p^N -> F_p^S has coordinate functions given by polynomials of total degree at most d. Then F is injective. If dS < N, no such F and decoder exist. Proof: At input 0 the decoder receives F(0) and must return a representation C computing zero. Both cases contradict its output C. Thus F is injective. Now put P_i(X)=F_i(X)-F_i(0), for i=1,...,S. These polynomials have degree at most d and their common zero set contains 0. If dS<N, their degree sum is less than N, so Chevalley–Warning says the number of common zeros in F_p^N is divisible by p. Since the set contains 0, it has at least p elements and therefore contains a nonzero x. For that x, F(x)=F(0), contradicting injectivity. Hence dS>=N is necessary. This concerns only the degree of the final map; per-stage degree bounds do not imply this hypothesis without a composition-degree bound.

statement_start: LEMMA (degree growth for staged polynomial updates). Let p be prime, S,N,T >= 1, and d >= 1.
statement: LEMMA (degree growth for staged polynomial updates). Let p be prime, S,N,T >= 1, and d >= 1. A deterministic streaming machine has S state coordinates over F_p, starts in a fixed state, and reads T symbols from F_p. Suppose each update coordinate is a polynomial of total degree at most d in the previous S state coordinates and the current input symbol. Then each final-state coordinate is represented by a polynomial of total degree at most d^T in the N=T input coordinates. If the machine has a deterministic exact search decoder depending on the input only through its final state, and the searched function class contains the zero function, then the final-state map is injective. Consequently, if d^T S < N, no such machine and decoder exist. Proof: Let q_t(x_1,...,x_t) denote the vector of state-coordinate functions after t symbols. At t=0 these are constants, of degree 0. Inductively, if every coordinate of q_t has degree at most d^t, each update coordinate is a sum of monomials of degree at most d in coordinates of q_t and x_{t+1}. Substitution yields degree at most d*d^t=d^{t+1}; reductions of polynomial functions over F_p cannot increase degree. Thus the final coordinates have degree at most d^T. For injectivity, the decoder at the zero input must return a circuit computing zero, since zero is in the searched class. If a distinct input x had the same final state, the decoder would return that same circuit on x, which does not compute x. Hence the final map is injective. Write its coordinates as F_i. The polynomials F_i(X)-F_i(0), i=1,...,S, have degree at most d^T and share the zero X=0. If S*d^T<N, Chevalley-Warning implies their common zero set has cardinality divisible by p; since it contains zero, it contains at least p points and hence a nonzero x. This contradicts injectivity. Therefore S*d^T>=N. Scope: the alphabet is F_p and each update is polynomial in the current symbol and state; no claim is made for arbitrary Boolean update circuits without a degree bound or for useful parameters when T is large.

statement: statement: LEMMA (range bound for exact search decoders on a valid input subfamily). Let X be finite, U⊆X consist only of inputs with valid witnesses, and let q:X→Q be the final state map of a deterministic streaming realization with decoder D:Q→W∪{⊥}. statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (R1, F_2-linear input-independent streaming; explicit YES convention). Let N be a positive integer and let s be a circuit-size threshold such that the constant-zero function has a circuit of size at most s. If an affine final state q(x)=Mx+c over F_2, with M in F_2^{S x N}, and a decoder correctly solve Search-MCSP[s] on every x in F_2^N, then S >= N.
proof: Let 0 denote the all-zero truth table. By the stated size condition, 0 is a YES instance, so correctness forces D(q(0)) to be a circuit C computing 0. Suppose k is a nonzero vector in ker(M). Then q(k)=Mk+c=c=q(0), hence the deterministic decoder returns the same C on k. Correctness on k requires C to compute the truth table k, whereas correctness on 0 requires C to compute 0. Since k != 0, these truth tables differ, contradiction. Thus ker(M)={0}; rank(M)=N. Since M has S rows, rank(M)<=S, giving S>=N.
gap: This proves the affine realization bound only. It does not establish the subfamily-counting obligation in Q-85e487150a: exhibiting a valid U of size p^{N-o(N)} among size-s circuit truth tables, nor transfer to unrestricted streaming realizations.

label: S0070
statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (Counting obstruction to the proposed large YES subfamily). In the fan-in-two DAG circuit model with m inputs and at most s gates, the number of distinct Boolean functions computable by circuits of size at most s is at most sum_{t=0}^s (m+t)16^t product_{j=0}^{t-1}(m+j)^2. Consequently, if s(m)=poly(m), N=2^m, and p>1 is fixed, then for every function epsilon(m)=o(N), there is no subfamily U of size p^{N-epsilon(m)} consisting of size-s(m) circuit truth tables.
proof: For a circuit with exactly t gates, order the gates topologically. At gate j (0-indexed), there are at most m+j available input wires; choosing two ordered predecessor wires gives at most (m+j)^2 possibilities, and choosing the gate type and any polarity conventions is bounded by 16. There are at most m+t choices of output wire. Thus the number of descriptions with t gates is at most (m+t)16^t product_{j=0}^{t-1}(m+j)^2. Summing over t<=s bounds the number of descriptions, hence also the number of distinct functions. Since m+j<=m+s, the sum is at most (s+1)(m+s)16^s(m+s)^{2s}; its base-2 logarithm is O(s log(m+s)). If s(m)=poly(m), this logarithm is poly(m)=o(2^m)=o(N). On the other hand log_2(p^{N-epsilon(m)})=(N-epsilon(m))log_2 p=Theta(N). For sufficiently large m the latter exceeds the logarithm of the circuit-count bound, so no such U exists.
gap: This rules out the proposed subfamily-count route for polynomial s. It does not establish a lower bound for unrestricted streaming realizations. The affine S0069 argument uses a separate kernel collision with the zero YES input.

statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (Affine-final-state lower bound for exact Search-MCSP on any circuit family containing zero). Let N>=1, let Y be any subset of {0,1}^N containing 0^N, and suppose a deterministic exact-search procedure has final state q(x)=Mx+c over F_2 with M in F_2^{S x N}, after which a decoder outputs a circuit computing x for x in Y and outputs NONE for x outside Y. Then S>=N.
proof: Since 0^N is in Y, exactness forces D(c) to be a circuit computing 0^N. If k is a nonzero vector in ker(M), then q(k)=Mk+c=c, so D(q(k))=D(c). If k is in Y, exactness requires this output circuit to compute k, contradicting k != 0^N; if k is outside Y, exactness requires NONE, also contradicting that D(c) is a circuit. Therefore ker(M)={0}, rank(M)=N, and S>=N. The argument uses only the affine final map and the fact that the decoder depends only on that final state; it allows arbitrary intermediate computation so long as the final state is affine in the full input.

statement: LEMMA (R1, affine F_2 exact search with explicit zero-circuit convention). Let N=2^m with m>=1. Suppose the circuit basis contains a constant-zero output of size at most s. label: S0076
statement:
statement: LEMMA (valid-input counting bound for deterministic exact search). Let F be any finite set of distinct Boolean functions on m inputs, each having a circuit of size at most s in a fixed circuit model. If a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm correctly solves Search-MCSP[s] on all truth tables in F and its decoder depends only on its final state, then it has at least |F| distinct final states, so S >= ceil(log_2 |F|). Proof: if distinct f,g in F reached the same final state, the decoder would return the same output on both; correctness requires that output to compute f and g respectively, impossible since f != g. In particular, the family f_{a,b}(x)=a·x+b over F_2, with a in F_2^m and b in F_2, contains exactly 2^(m+1) distinct functions: their values at 0 and the m unit vectors recover b and every coordinate of a. Thus S >= m+1 whenever s includes circuits for this family.
evidence: The argument proves injectivity of the state map on every valid input family. The affine family cardinality follows by recovering its parameters from m+1 evaluations. This is an explicit attainable family, but it does not meet G0004's near-2^N target.

label: S0078
statement:
statement: LEMMA (affine F_p exact-search collision bound). Let p be prime, N,S≥0, and q(x)=Mx+c for x∈{0,1}^N, with M∈F_p^{S×N}. Suppose a decoder depending only on q(x) solves exact Search-MCSP on every N-bit truth table, and a size-at-most-s circuit for 0^N exists. Then N≤S(p−1). Proof: Let v_1,…,v_N be the columns of M and G=(F_p)^S. In the group algebra A=F_p[G], write y_j=X_j−1 for the coordinate generators. Then A≅F_p[y_1,…,y_S]/(y_1^p,…,y_S^p), so the augmentation ideal I=(y_1,…,y_S) satisfies I^{S(p−1)+1}=0. Each 1−X^{v_i} lies in I. If N>S(p−1), then ∏_i(1−X^{v_i})=0. In its group-basis expansion, the coefficient of X^0 is the sum of (−1)^{|J|} over subsets J⊆[N] with ∑_{i∈J}v_i=0. The empty subset contributes 1; if no nonempty such J existed, that coefficient would be 1, contradicting the zero product. Hence some nonempty J has zero column sum. Its indicator k∈{0,1}^N is nonzero and Mk=0, so q(k)=q(0). Exact decoding at 0^N must return a circuit computing 0^N; the same output at k is incorrect because k≠0^N. Contradiction. Thus N≤S(p−1), or S≥ceil(N/(p−1)).
evidence: The complete proof is the nilpotent-augmentation-ideal argument in the statement. Independent exhaustive verification cm-925ab4d686cf4720 checked all sequences for p=2,3; S=1,2; N=S(p−1)+1,+2, with no counterexample (largest case: 531441 sequences). The computation is a finite check only.

statement: REPAIR (decision-only affine period bound; not a search lemma). Let N be the truth-table length and let A⊆{0,1}^N be any set containing 0^N. Suppose a deterministic decoder D reads only q(x)=Mx+c, where M∈F_2^{S×N}, and correctly decides membership in A on every x∈{0,1}^N: D(q(x))=1 iff x∈A. Define P={k∈F_2^N: 1_A(x+k)=1_A(x) for every x∈F_2^N}. Then ker(M)⊆P and S≥N−dim(P)≥N−log_2|A|. Proof: If Mk=0, then q(x+k)=M(x+k)+c=Mx+c=q(x) for every x. Because D depends only on q, membership is invariant under adding k, so k∈P. P is a subgroup: it contains 0 and is closed under addition by composing its invariances. Since 0^N∈A, every k∈P also lies in A; hence |P|≤|A| and dim(P)≤log_2|A|. Rank-nullity gives S≥rank(M)=N−dim ker(M)≥N−dim(P)≥N−log_2|A|. This is only a decision lower bound for affine final states and final-state-only decoding; it does not establish the corresponding search statement.

(b) If k has circuit size>s, D(q_N(k)) must be 'none', but it is C_0 (a circuit), contradiction. Either way contradiction, so N<=S(p-1).

statement_start: LEMMA (Candidate A affine staged realization lower bound over F_2). Let N = 2^m. statement: LEMMA (YES-fiber bound for affine streaming search). Let Y be the set of YES inputs in a finite search problem with inputs in F_2^N. Suppose a one-pass streaming machine has fixed affine updates and final state q(x)=Ax+c in F_2^S, followed by a deterministic decoder that outputs a correct witness for every x in Y. Then A is injective on Y and S >= ceil(log_2 |Y|). Proof: if x,y in Y and Ax=Ay, then q(x)=q(y), so the decoder returns the same output on both. Correctness would require that output to witness both inputs. For Search-MCSP, a circuit computes a unique truth table, so distinct x,y cannot share a correct circuit. Thus A is injective on Y. Therefore |Y| <= |im A| = 2^rank(A) <= 2^S, proving the bound. The decoder may be any deterministic function, including an oracle-aided decoder.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (YES-fiber injectivity for affine exact search). Let X be a finite subset of F_2^N, let Y subseteq X be the YES inputs, and let W be a witness set with relation R subseteq Y x W. Suppose every x in Y has at least one valid witness and the valid-witness sets W_x={w in W:R(x,w)} are pairwise disjoint for distinct x in Y. Let q(x)=Ax+c in F_2^S, where A is an S-by-N matrix over F_2 and c in F_2^S, and let D:F_2^S -> W union {none} be deterministic with D(q(x)) in W_x for every x in Y. Then q is injective on Y and S >= ceil(log_2 |Y|) (with the bound interpreted as 0 if Y is empty). Proof: Take distinct x,y in Y. If q(x)=q(y), determinism gives D(q(x))=D(q(y))=w. Correctness on YES inputs implies w is a valid witness for both, so w belongs to W_x intersect W_y, contradicting pairwise disjointness. Thus q is injective on Y. Since q(x)=Ax+c, injectivity of q on Y implies injectivity of A on Y. Therefore |Y| <= |im(A)|=2^rank(A) <= 2^S, and taking base-2 logarithms gives S >= ceil(log_2 |Y|). The decoder's output on X\Y is irrelevant, so it may output none there.

For Search-MCSP, valid circuit witnesses for distinct truth tables are disjoint because a circuit computes a unique truth table. This repairs the none-output issue but yields only the YES-set counting bound, not S >= N.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (bounded witness multiplicity fiber bound). Let X and Y be finite sets with Y subseteq X, let W be a witness set, and let R be a subset of Y times W. For x in Y define W_x={w in W:(x,w) in R}. Assume each x in Y has at least one valid witness. Define L=max over w in W of |{x in Y:w in W_x}|. Let q:X->F_2^S be any state map and D:F_2^S->{none} union W be deterministic, with D(q(x)) in W_x for every x in Y. If Y is nonempty, then |Y|<=L*2^S and hence S>=ceil(log_2(|Y|/L)). Proof: For each state z in q(Y), correctness implies D(z)=w_z in W. Every x in the fiber {x in Y:q(x)=z} must then satisfy w_z in W_x. By the definition of L, this fiber has at most L elements. The fibers over q(Y) partition Y, so |Y|<=L*|q(Y)|<=L*2^S. Since Y is nonempty and every YES input has a witness, L>=1. Taking base-two logarithms and using integral S gives the stated ceiling bound. The result does not require q to be affine.
evidence: Complete fiber-counting proof supplied in the statement. It generalizes pairwise-disjoint witness sets (L=1) to bounded witness multiplicity; it does not assert a strong MCSP state lower bound without a useful bound on L.
gap: For Search-MCSP, determine whether a useful upper bound on the number of size-<=s circuits computing any one truth table yields a nontrivial |Y|/L bound in the exact realization model. This counting lemma alone does not close the manuscript's stronger target.
refuted_approach: The earlier YES-only disjoint-witness lemma does not apply when one witness may be valid for several inputs. The bounded-multiplicity hypothesis captures that overlap explicitly.

statement: LEMMA (staged affine exact-search lower bound over a prime field, REPAIRED). Let p be prime, N,S ≥ 0. Consider a one-pass streaming algorithm with state q_t ∈ F_p^S evolving on input x = (x_1,...,x_N) ∈ {0,1}^N by q_0 = c_0 and q_t = M_t q_{t-1} + x_t v_t + c_t for t = 1..N, where M_t ∈ F_p^{S×S}, v_t,c_t ∈ F_p^S are fixed (input-independent). Let q_N(x) = M x + c with M ∈ F_p^{S×N}, c ∈ F_p^S. Let D: F_p^S → {circuits of size ≤ s over the full binary basis {AND,OR,NOT,0,1}} ∪ {'none'} be a decoder. Correctness: ∀x ∈ {0,1}^N, if x has a circuit of size ≤ s then D(q_N(x)) is a circuit computing x; else D(q_N(x)) = 'none'. Assume the constant-0 function on N bits has a circuit of size ≤ s (true for s ≥ 1 with constants as size-1 gates). Then N ≤ S(p-1). Equivalently, S ≥ ⌈N/(p-1)⌉. Proof: (1) By induction, q_t is affine in x_1..x_t, so q_N(x)=Mx+c. Let w_i ∈ F_p^S be the columns of M. (2) In the group algebra A = F_p[(Z/pZ)^S] ≅ F_p[y_1,...,y_S]/(y_1^p,...,y_S^p), the augmentation ideal I=(y_1,...,y_S) satisfies I^{S(p-1)+1}=0 because any monomial of total degree ≥ S(p-1)+1 has some y_j with exponent ≥ p. (3) Each 1 - X^{w_i} ∈ I since X_j = 1+y_j. If N > S(p-1), then ∏_{i=1}^N (1 - X^{w_i}) ∈ I^N = 0. (4) Expand: ∏(1-X^{w_i}) = ∑_{J⊆[N]} (-1)^{|J|} X^{∑_{i∈J} w_i}. The coefficient of X^0 is ∑_{J: ∑_{i∈J} w_i=0} (-1)^{|J|}. The empty set contributes +1. If no nonempty J has zero column sum, the coefficient is 1 ≠ 0, contradicting the product being 0. Thus ∃ nonempty J⊆[N] with ∑_{i∈J} w_i = 0. (5) Let k ∈ {0,1}^N be the indicator of J. Then k ≠ 0 and M k = 0, so q_N(k) = q_N(0) = c. (6) Since 0^N has a size-≤s circuit, D(c) = C_0 where C_0 computes the constant-0 function. By correctness, D(q_N(k)) = D(c) = C_0. But C_0 computes 0^N ≠ k. If k is a YES instance, D(q_N(k)) should compute k ≠ 0^N. If k is a NO instance, D(q_N(k)) should be 'none'. Either way contradicts correctness. Therefore N ≤ S(p-1). ∎

label: S0120
statement: LEMMA (R1, F_2-linear/affine staged realization, SEARCH version, REPAIRED). Let N = 2^m. Let SearchMCSP[s] be the total search problem: on input x ∈ {0,1}^N, output a circuit of size ≤ s over the full binary basis {AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1} (constants 0 and 1 count as size-1 gates) that computes x, or output 'none' if no such circuit exists. Let s ≥ 1 (so the constant-0 function on N bits has a circuit of size 1 ≤ s). Consider a one-pass streaming algorithm with affine state updates over F_2: q_0 = c_0, q_t = M_t q_{t-1} + L_t x_t + c_t for t = 1..N (fixed M_t ∈ F_2^{S×S}, L_t ∈ F_2^{S×1}, c_t ∈ F_2^S). Final state q_N = M x + c with M ∈ F_2^{S×N}, c ∈ F_2^S. Decoder D: F_2^S → {circuits of size ≤ s} ∪ {'none'}. Correctness: ∀x ∈ {0,1}^N, if x has circuit size ≤ s then D(q_N(x)) is a circuit computing x; else D(q_N(x)) = 'none'. Then S ≥ N = 2^m. Proof: (1) By induction, q_t is affine in x_1..x_t, so q_N(x) = Mx + c. (2) The all-zero truth table 0^N has the constant-0 circuit of size 1 ≤ s, so it is a YES instance. By correctness, D(q_N(0)) = D(c) = C_0 where C_0 computes the constant-0 function. (3) Suppose for contradiction that ker M ≠ {0}. Let k ∈ ker M, k ≠ 0. Then q_N(k) = Mk + c = c = q_N(0). By correctness, D(q_N(k)) = D(c) = C_0. (4) Case analysis: (a) If k has circuit size ≤ s, then D(q_N(k)) must be a circuit computing k. But D(q_N(k)) = C_0 computes 0^N ≠ k (since k ≠ 0). Contradiction. (b) If k has circuit size > s, then D(q_N(k)) must be 'none'. But D(q_N(k)) = C_0 is a circuit. Contradiction. (5) Therefore ker M = {0}. So rank M = N. Since M has S rows, S ≥ rank M = N = 2^m. ∎

statement: statement: For prime p, let A be an S×N matrix over F_p and q(x)=Ax+c for x∈{0,1}^N. If a final-state decoder correctly solves exact SearchMCSP[s] on all N-bit truth tables and 0^N has circuit size ≤s, then N≤S(p−1). Proof: Write A's columns as v_1,…,v_N∈F_p^S. If N>S(p−1), the augmentation ideal J of F_p[(Z/pZ)^S] satisfies J^{S(p−1)+1}=0: it is generated by y_j=X^{e_j}−1, with y_j^p=0. Thus ∏_i(1−X^{v_i})=0. Its identity coefficient is the signed sum over subsets whose column sum is zero; if no nonempty subset summed to zero, that coefficient would be 1, a contradiction. So some nonempty I has Σ_{i∈I}v_i=0. For k=1_I, Ak=0 and q(k)=q(0). Correctness at zero makes the decoder output a circuit computing 0^N. The same output on k is invalid: if k has size ≤s it must compute k≠0^N; otherwise the decoder must output none. Hence N≤S(p−1). Scope: affine F_p final-state maps with 0^N a yes-instance; nonlinear updates are not covered.

statement: REPAIRED R1 prime-field affine search lemma. Fix a prime p, integers N,S>=0, and a circuit convention under which the zero truth table has a size-at-most-s circuit. Any exact one-pass affine streaming realization with state q_t in F_p^S, fixed updates q_t=M_t q_{t-1}+x_t v_t+c_t for x_t in {0,1}, and a decoder that must output a circuit computing x on every yes input (and may output none on no inputs), requires N <= S(p-1). Proof: composing the fixed affine updates gives q_N(x)=Mx+c for an S-by-N matrix M over F_p. Let w_i be its columns. In the group algebra A=F_p[(Z/pZ)^S], let X^u denote the group element for u. The augmentation ideal I is generated by X^{e_j}-1, and A is isomorphic to F_p[y_1,...,y_S]/(y_1^p,...,y_S^p), via y_j=X^{e_j}-1; hence I^{S(p-1)+1}=0. Every 1-X^{w_i} belongs to I. If N>S(p-1), then the product over i of (1-X^{w_i}) vanishes. Its expansion is the sum over subsets J of (-1)^|J| X^{sum_{i in J}w_i}. If no nonempty subset J had sum zero, the coefficient of the identity group element would be exactly 1 (from J=empty), contradicting the zero product. Thus a nonempty J has sum zero. Its nonzero binary indicator k satisfies Mk=0, so q_N(k)=q_N(0). Since zero is a yes instance, the decoder output at q_N(0) is a circuit computing 0; the same output at k would have to compute k, impossible for k != 0. Therefore N<=S(p-1). This is a restricted-model result only; it makes no claim about nonlinear updates or unrestricted PNP lower bounds.

label: S0134
statement: statement: Lemma (affine prime-field search bound). Let p be prime and let N,S be nonnegative integers. An input x in {0,1}^N is processed by q_0=c_0 and q_t=M_t q_{t-1}+x_t v_t+c_t in F_p^S, with fixed M_t,v_t,c_t. Suppose the final-state decoder exactly solves a search problem whose zero input is a yes-instance, and every output on a yes-instance must compute that input. Then N<=S(p-1). Proof. Composing the affine updates gives q_N(x)=Mx+c for an S-by-N matrix M over F_p. Write its columns as w_1,...,w_N. In A=F_p[(Z/pZ)^S], let X^u denote the basis element indexed by u, and let I be the augmentation ideal. The standard presentation A=F_p[y_1,...,y_S]/(y_1^p,...,y_S^p), with y_j=X^{e_j}-1, gives I^{S(p-1)+1}=0. Each factor 1-X^{w_i} lies in I. If N>S(p-1), their product is zero. Expanding gives sum over J subset [N] of (-1)^|J| X^{sum_{i in J} w_i}=0. If no nonempty J had sum zero, the coefficient of X^0 would be 1, contributed only by the empty set, contradicting the zero product. Thus some nonempty J has sum of columns zero. Its nonzero binary indicator k satisfies Mk=0, hence q_N(k)=q_N(0). The decoder must output the same object on 0 and k. Its output on 0 computes the zero input, so it cannot compute the distinct input k, contradicting correctness on the yes input k if k is yes; if k is no, exactness instead requires the decoder to report none, also contradicting its required yes-output at 0. Therefore N<=S(p-1). This is restricted to affine updates; it asserts no bound for nonlinear updates.

Final state q_N = M x + c with M in F_2^{S x N}, c in F_2^S. Decoder D: F_2^S -> {circuits of size <= s} U {'none'}. Correctness: for all x, if x has circuit size <= s then D(q_N(x)) is a circuit computing x; else D(q_N(x)) = 'none'. Then S >= N = 2^m. Proof: The all-zero truth table 0^N has circuit size 1 (single leaf 0), and 1 <= s since s >= 1. Thus it is a YES instance. So D(q_N(0)) = D(c) = C_0, a circuit computing the constant 0 function. Now suppose k in ker M, k != 0. Then q_N(k) = M k + c = c = q_N(0). By correctness, D(q_N(k)) = D(c) = C_0. But C_0 computes the constant 0 function. For this to be the correct output on input k, we would need k to be the constant 0 function, i.e., k = 0^N. Contradiction since k != 0. Therefore ker M = {0}. Hence rank M = N. Since M has S rows, S >= rank M = N = 2^m. QED.

Suppose 0 is a yes-instance of a search problem whose exact decoder depends only on q(x) and outputs a witness computing x on every yes-instance. Then N<=S(p-1), hence S>=ceil(N/(p-1)). statement: statement: Lemma (affine exact-search counting bound). Let p be prime and let N,S be nonnegative integers. Suppose an exact search problem on every x in {0,1}^N has a yes/no status and, on yes inputs, its decoder must output a witness that determines x uniquely (in particular, a circuit computing the truth table x); on no inputs it outputs a distinguished symbol NONE. Suppose the final state is q(x)=Mx+c in F_p^S and the decoder depends only on q(x). Then 2^N <= p^S, hence S >= ceil(N/log_2(p)). Proof: If q(x)=q(y), the decoder outputs the same value on x,y. If one is yes and one no, that value would have to be both a witness and NONE, impossible. If both are yes, the same witness would have to determine both x and y, so x=y. If both are no, q need not distinguish them. Therefore this argument alone does not imply injectivity on all inputs; restrict to the yes set Y to obtain |Y| <= p^S and S >= log_p |Y|. For Search-MCSP[s], this gives S >= log_p(number of N-bit truth tables of circuit size <=s), provided the decoder's witness uniquely determines its truth table. In the special case where every input is a yes instance, |Y|=2^N and the stated 2^N <= p^S follows. This lemma is deliberately scoped to the yes-set counting bound; it does not claim S >= N/log_2(p) for ordinary Search-MCSP.

statement: statement: Lemma (affine exact-search yes-set counting). Let p be prime and N,S be nonnegative integers. Let Y be the yes set of an exact search problem on inputs {0,1}^N. Suppose the final state is q(x)=Mx+c in F_p^S, the decoder depends only on q(x), and every output witness that is valid on a yes input uniquely determines that input. Then |Y| <= p^S, and therefore S >= ceil(log_p |Y|) when |Y|>0. Proof: If x,y in Y have q(x)=q(y), the decoder returns the same output on both.
