statement_start: LEMMA (repaired R1 affine exact-search bound). Let p be prime, N,S>=0, and let a one-pass stream have state q_t in F_p^S with fixed affine updates q_t=M_t q_{t-1}+x_t v_t+c_t for binary input bits x_t. Assume its final-state-only decoder exactly solves Search-MCSP[s] on all N-bit truth tables and the zero truth table has a circuit of size at most s. Then N<=S(p-1), so S>=ceil(N/(p-1)).
proof: Induction on t gives q_N(x)=Mx+c for a matrix M over F_p. Write w_i for its columns. The identity q_N(k)=q_N(0) for k in ker(M) intersect {0,1}^N implies k=0: exact correctness at 0 requires the decoder's output to compute 0^N, while the same output at k must compute k. Thus no nonempty subset of the columns w_i sums to zero in F_p^S. In the group algebra A=F_p[(Z/pZ)^S], let X^w denote the group basis element indexed by w. The augmentation ideal I is generated by y_j=X^{e_j}-1 and A is isomorphic to F_p[y_1,...,y_S]/(y_1^p,...,y_S^p), so I^{S(p-1)+1}=0. Each (1-X^{w_i}) lies in I. If N>S(p-1), their product is zero. Its coefficient at the identity is the sum over subsets J with sum_{i in J}w_i=0 of (-1)^|J|. By the no-nonempty-zero-sum property this coefficient equals 1 from J=emptyset, contradiction. Hence N<=S(p-1).

statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (finite-extension affine exact-search bound). Let p be prime and r,S,N be nonnegative integers. If a one-pass system has state in F_{p^r}^S, fixed affine updates driven by N binary bits, and a final-state-only decoder that exactly solves Search-MCSP on all N-bit truth tables, and the zero table is a yes-instance, then N <= rS(p-1).
statement: Let p be prime and r,S,N be nonnegative integers. Consider a one-pass system with state in F_{p^r}^S, fixed affine input-independent updates on N binary input bits, and output determined only by the final state. Suppose it exactly solves Search-MCSP[s] on all N-bit truth tables, and the zero truth table has a circuit of size at most s. Then N <= rS(p-1). Proof: Composing the affine updates gives q(x)=Mx+c over F_{p^r}. Regard the additive group of F_{p^r}^S as (Z/pZ)^{rS}, and let w_i be the columns of M. If a nonempty subset J of columns sums to zero, its indicator vector k in {0,1}^N is nonzero and q(k)=q(0). At zero the decoder must return a circuit computing 0^N. On k, the same output is incorrect: if k is a yes-instance, that circuit would have to compute k, whereas it computes 0^N; if k is a no-instance, the decoder would have to return none. Thus no nonempty subset of the columns sums to zero. In A=F_p[(Z/pZ)^{rS}], the augmentation ideal I is generated by y_j=X^{e_j}-1 and A is isomorphic to F_p[y_1,...,y_{rS}]/(y_1^p,...,y_{rS}^p), so I^{rS(p-1)+1}=0. Each 1-X^{w_i} lies in I. If N>rS(p-1), then product_i(1-X^{w_i})=0. Its identity coefficient is the sum of (-1)^|J| over subsets J whose columns sum to zero. Since only the empty subset does so, this coefficient is 1, contradiction. Therefore N<=rS(p-1).

statement_start: LEMMA (state-count bound for exact Search-MCSP). Let p be prime and r,S,N be nonnegative integers.
statement: Let p be prime and r,S,N be nonnegative integers. Any exact final-state-only Search-MCSP decoder on all N-bit truth tables with state space F_{p^r}^S requires 2^N <= p^(rS), hence N <= rS log_2(p). Proof: if two distinct input truth tables x,y yield the same state, the decoder must give the same output for both. A circuit computes exactly one truth table, so cannot be a valid search output for both distinct tables; the output 'none' cannot be correct on the zero table, which is a yes-instance, and another distinct input simultaneously. Thus the final-state map is injective on {0,1}^N. Counting states gives 2^N <= p^(rS). This argument does not require affine updates.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (injective-output collision principle). Let X be a finite input set, Q a state set, and D:Q -> Y a deterministic decoder. Suppose a streaming realization maps each input x to final state h(x), and correctness requires D(h(x)) to be a valid output for x. If there is an input x0 such that no output valid for x0 is valid for any distinct x in X, then h is injective. Consequently |Q| >= |X|. For an affine final state h(x)=Mx+c over F_2 on X=F_2^N, this implies rank(M)=N and the state dimension S is at least N.
proof: Assume h(x)=h(x0) for some x distinct from x0. Determinism gives D(h(x))=D(h(x0)). Correctness makes this output valid for both x and x0, contradicting the hypothesis that their valid-output sets are disjoint. Hence h is injective. Therefore |Q|>=|X|. In the affine F_2 case, h(x)=Mx+c; injectivity implies ker(M)={0}, so rank(M)=N. Since M has S rows, rank(M)<=S, hence S>=N.
scope: This is a finite-set collision lemma. For Search-MCSP, the valid outputs are circuits computing the input or none; the valid-output sets for distinct inputs are disjoint, provided the problem's correctness specification is exact. The affine specialization recovers the state-dimension bound when the affine map is defined on all F_2^N. It gives no lower bound for general nonlinear realizations beyond |Q|>=|X| when their final state is itself the bounded resource.

statement: LEMMA (affine exact-search state bound over any finite field). Let F be a finite field, X=F^N, and h:X->F^S be affine. Suppose a deterministic decoder returns an output valid for x, with valid-output sets for distinct x pairwise disjoint. Then S>=N. Proof: If h(x)=h(y), the deterministic decoder returns the same output on x and y, contradicting disjointness unless x=y. Thus h is injective. Writing h(x)=Mx+c, injectivity implies ker M={0}; rank-nullity gives rank M=N, and rank M<=S. Hence S>=N. This covers exact search tasks with uniquely identifying witnesses when the final state is affine. It does not cover nonlinear updates.

statement: LEMMA (YES-fiber state bound for exact search). Let X be finite, Y subset X be the YES inputs, Q a finite state set, h:X->Q the final-state map, and D:Q->O a deterministic decoder. Suppose every y in Y has a valid output identifying y uniquely: no output valid for y is valid for a distinct y' in Y. Then |Q| >= |Y|. Proof: If distinct y,y' in Y had h(y)=h(y'), determinism gives D(h(y))=D(h(y')); that output would be valid for both, contradicting unique identification. Hence h restricted to Y is injective, so its image has |Y| elements and is contained in Q. For Search-MCSP, a circuit output identifies its truth table, so this gives at least as many final states as size-at-most-s truth tables. It does not constrain collisions between NO inputs or imply an exponential-in-N state bound without a lower bound on |Y|.
proof: For y,y' in Y with h(y)=h(y'), determinism makes the decoded output identical. By the hypothesis that a valid output for y cannot be valid for a distinct y' in Y, this forces y=y'. Thus h is injective on Y and |Q|>=|h(Y)|=|Y|.
gap: The size of the YES set in the target parameter regime and the nonlinear-update case remain open.

label: S0157
statement:
statement: LEMMA (affine-function YES-set count). For m>=1 and s>=m, if the circuit basis includes XOR and each two-input XOR costs one gate, Search-MCSP on m-input Boolean functions has at least 2^(m+1) YES truth tables: all affine functions a·x xor b. Each is computed with at most m XOR gates (omit zero terms; use the constant b), and they are distinct because evaluation at 0 and the m unit vectors recovers b and each coefficient a_i. Consequently any exact search realization whose decoder outputs a uniquely identifying witness on each YES input requires at least 2^(m+1) final states.
proof: For each (a,b) in {0,1}^m x {0,1}, form f_(a,b)(x)=a·x xor b. At most m-1 gates combine the selected variables and one additional gate incorporates b when needed, so the total is at most m; constant and zero cases use no more gates. If f_(a,b)=f_(a',b'), evaluating at 0 gives b=b'; evaluating at e_i then gives a_i=a'_i for every i. Thus there are 2^(m+1) distinct YES functions. A deterministic exact-search decoder cannot assign the same state to two such inputs because its single output circuit would have to compute both distinct functions. Hence there are at least 2^(m+1) final states.
gap: This gives only m+1 state bits and assumes XOR is a unit-cost gate. It does not establish the N=2^m affine-state lower bound or address nonlinear updates.

label: S0001
statement: QO1 UPPER BOUND UNDER NP in P/poly (derivation of the OPS21 Thm 1.4 mechanism, author Claude family): NP subset SIZE[n^a] => there is K=K(a) such that for EVERY s=s(n) with n <= s <= 2^{n/2}: Gap-MCSP[s/(cn), s] on N=2^n bits has circuits of size N*s^K (a.e.). Proof: s'=s/(cn). Greedy anti-checker: V_0 = all circuits of size <= s', Y_0 = empty. Step i: for every position y in [N] (a fixed wire x_y) evaluate an approximate count of |{C in V_i: C(y) != x_y}|/|V_i| given (Y_i, x|Y_i, y, x_y) - input length L = O(t n), Stockmeyer approximate counting is in BPP^NP subset Sigma_3 subset P/poly (Karp-Lipton chain) so size L^{a'}; a tournament over the N candidates picks the best (y, x_y): N*L^{a'} gates per step. Elimination: if CC(x) > s then for every nonempty V_i some y kills >= 1/3 of V_i (minimax on V_i: otherwise a distribution over V_i is correct w.p. > 2/3 on every input and the majority of O(n) samples computes x with size O(n s') <= s, contradiction); with approximation >= 1/4. Hence V_t = empty after t = O(s' log s') steps. YES (CC(x) <= s'): the circuit for x is never eliminated. Final test 'V_t empty' is coNP on L bits. Total t*N*L^{a'} = N*s^{K}, K = a'+2, independent of s and beta. With s = N^beta: g_beta(N) <= N^{1+K beta} for all beta in (0,1/2]. c is the constant from the majority step (not necessarily 10).

statement: QO2 WEAKEST SUFFICIENT QUANTIFIER FORM Q*: if for every K >= 1 there is a size function s_K (n <= s_K <= 2^{n/2}) such that Gap-MCSP[s_K/(cn), s_K] has no circuits of size N*s_K^K for infinitely many n, then NP notsubset P/poly, hence P != NP (contrapositive of QO1). Special cases: Q1 (exists eps, all small beta: g_beta notin O(N^{1+eps})) => Q2 (for all k, delta exists beta < delta: g_beta notin O(N^{1+k beta}); take beta < min(delta, eps/k)) => Q* (s_K = N^beta). Q3 (fixed s = n^c, g notin O(N log^k N) for all k) => Q*. Lower bounds whose exponent ratio eps(beta)/beta is bounded (eps = beta, 2 beta) do NOT suffice since K is unknown; eps = sqrt(beta), beta log(1/beta) or N*(log N)^{omega(1)} at s = polylog do. LOCALITY (CHOPRS20): the QO1 circuits are N*poly(s) wires into fan-in-poly(s) PH predicates, so any proof of Q* must fail against such oracle circuits.

label: S0004
statement: AF (conditional, replaces the size budget by a correlation budget): let beta in (0,1), eta>0. Assume (P1) a local PRG fooling De Morgan formulas of size s with error delta <= 2^{-gamma}/10, seed and per-bit circuit size <= N^{beta-eta}; (P2) a pseudorandom restriction rho with >= N^{beta+eta/2} stars such that, w.p. >= 0.9, the principal-formula forest Phi of C|rho (reused-gate leaves kept as never-restricted variables) has size <= s. Then Gap-MCSP[N^beta] has no gamma-almost-formula of size S. Proof: fix such rho; YES = G(z) o rho has circuit size <= N^beta, NO = random fill has circuit size >= N^{beta+eta/2-o(1)} w.p. 1-2^{-N^{Omega(1)}}, so Adv(C|rho) >= 1/2; by D4 some F_a of size <= s has advantage >= 2^{-gamma-1} > delta, contradicting P1. BUDGET: gamma <= log2(1/delta) - 4 instead of r + log2(2S+1) <= 3 beta log2 N; since any PRG needs seed >= log(1/delta), gamma can reach N^{beta-eta} (polynomial) instead of O(log N).

label: S0059
statement:
T11-D: REFUTATION of an unverified padded-permanent multiplicity table (gpt-oss-120b, NOT_VERIFIED) AND a course-correction on obstruction-hunting. (a) The model claimed a_{(5,1)}=1 for the padded perm_2 at (m,n,d)=(2,3,2). CONTAINMENT ARGUMENT: dc(perm_2)=2 <= 3, so the padded perm_2 = l^1 perm_2 lies IN the orbit closure of det_3 (Z_{2,3} subset D_3); restriction C[D_3] ->> C[Z_{2,3}] is surjective, giving a_lambda <= delta_lambda <= g(lambda,(d^n),(d^n)) for ALL lambda. My VERIFIED g((5,1),(2,2,2),(2,2,2))=0 (T11-C) therefore forces a_{(5,1)}=0, contradicting the table. Table rejected. (b) COURSE-CORRECTION: the case (m,n)=(2,3) is DEGENERATE for obstruction-hunting - since perm_2 is contained in closure(det_3), NO separation exists, so NO occurrence OR multiplicity obstruction can exist there by definition. label: S0069
statement:
REJECTED: the proposed extension of the null-cone lemma to NON-rectangular partitions, and the claimed d_min^sep(3,4) >= 9. MATH ERROR: for a non-rectangular lambda with ell=k, the HWV transforms as P_lambda(g(t).f) = t^w P_lambda(f) with w = k*lambda_1 - |lambda| != 0. Then lim_{t->0} t^w P_lambda(f) = 0 for w>0 holds for ANY value of P_lambda(f), giving NO information - one CANNOT conclude P_lambda(f)=0. The null-cone argument works ONLY for w=0 (rectangular lambda=(d^k) = SL_k-invariant), where P_lambda(g(t).f)=P_lambda(f) is constant so P_lambda(f)=P_lambda(0)=0. ADVERSARIAL CONFIRMATION (exact computation): lambda=(12,2,2,2,2) has w=5*12-20=40>0; the flawed lemma predicts vanishing on Y, but the HWV evaluates NONZERO on z*perm_3 (e.g. 103363705/13824, 1785096875/27 at random 5-planes) => delta_perm=1, consistent with my original d=5 report (22 of 23 five-row HWVs non-vanishing on perm). Direct contradiction => extension invalid. CORRECTED STATUS: only d_min^sep(3,4) >= 6 stands (from rectangular T11-N + BHIM symmetroid bound for ell<=4 up to degree 8 + the 23 five-row d=5 certificates). d_min^sep(3,4) >= 9 is NOT proven. LMR PRECISIONS (owner): LMR Thm 3.1.1 gives degree-2n(n-1) equations but does NOT prove this is the MINIMAL separation degree; LMR equations are not automatically certified separators without checking non-vanishing on Y; the Hessian criterion concerns rank at points of the hypersurface {f=0}, not the whole space (Hess(det_n) at the identity is non-degenerate). So 'degree 24 = proven minimum' is unjustified. VALID OPEN TASK: for d=6,7,8 and non-rectangular ell>=5 partitions, determine structurally whether ker E_D not subset ker E_Y can occur; no valid null-cone shortcut exists for the non-rectangular case.

label: S0070
statement:
VALID structural restriction (owner, replacing the rejected null-cone extension): for Y_{m,n} and ANY partition lambda, lambda_1 < d(n-m) => P_lambda|_{Y_{m,n}} == 0. (Divisibility/weight argument, NOT null-cone.)
PREMISES: Any k-plane restriction f|_U = u_1^{n-m} * C_m (C_m = perm_m|_U), so every coefficient c_alpha of f|_U with alpha_1 < n-m is zero; A degree-d HWV P_lambda is a sum of monomials c_{alpha^(1)}...c_{alpha^(d)} with total u_1-weight sum_j alpha^(j)_1 = lambda_1; If lambda_1 < d(n-m) then by pigeonhole some factor has alpha^(j)_1 < n-m, which is 0 at f|_U => every monomial vanishes => P_lambda(f|_U)=0 for EVERY U => P_lambda|_Y == 0; EDGE case lambda_1 = d(n-m): every factor must have alpha_1 = n-m exactly, so evaluation collapses to P_lambda(u_1^{n-m} * Cbar_m) where Cbar_m = C_m(0,u_2,...,u_k) in k-1 variables (dimension reduction)
PROOF:

label: S0071
statement:
Padding-floor EQUIVALENCE REFUTED (certified counterexample, independently verified); proven (<=) direction retained; replaced by a TWO-CONDITION necessary filter. COUNTEREXAMPLE (owner): (m,n,d)=(2,3,6), lambda=(8,2,2,2,2,2)|-18 has p_lambda>0 and lambda_1=8 >= d(n-m)=6, but gamma_lambda(Y_{2,3})=0. MECHANISM: the HWV P(F)=det((A_{1ij})_{1<=i,j<=6}) (6x6 contraction of the cubic's symmetric coefficient tensor) has weight (8,2,2,2,2,2); the padded permanent z*perm_2 uses only m^2+1=5 essential variables, so the 6x6 contraction has rank<=5 and determinant 0 => vanishes on all of Y_{2,3}. Not identically zero: F_0=x_1^3+3x_1(x_2^2+..+x_6^2) gives contraction=I_6, P(F_0)=1. VERIFIED by exact sympy: z*perm_2 -> rank 4 det 0; random g.f -> rank 5 det 0; F_0 -> rank 6 det 6^6. Generalizes (r=m^2+2) to an infinite counterexample family; subspace-variety geometry (classical, Landsberg). label: S0083
statement:
Slice route: level-m slices of f_n are coNP-hard (padding); monotone and general circuit size are polynomially related on slices (Berkowitz), so a superpolynomial monotone bound for them would prove P != NP (equivalent reformulation). Span-program analogue: mSP and SP polynomially related on slices, loss SP >= (mSP - 2N)/(N-1): all PNP-001 bounds (<= N+1) vanish under transfer. Generic Gal constructions on slices are natural-proofs-blocked (assuming NC^1 PRFs); a method must use function-specific structure.
PREMISES: Berkowitz 1982 (cited)

label: S0087
statement:
For positive 1-in-3, fixing a single variable never makes a GF(3)-consistent system inconsistent (the solution set is invariant under +lambda*j, so each coordinate takes all values). Hence the least depth of a case-split tree whose leaves are refuted by GF(3) consistency is 0 or >= 2; observed values 0, 2, 3 only (n=4..12). Open: the growth of this depth with n (needs a lower-bound argument, not samples); it is a measure for the algorithm class 'DPLL + GF(3) Gaussian elimination', not for circuits.
PREMISES: D-018 (T44 C1: j in kernel over GF(3)); RC-45241185 measurements (retracted for the growth claim only)
PROOF:

statement:

label: S0092
statement:
Generalization of the two-value criterion to positive 1-in-k over GF(p): (i) the all-ones vector j is in the kernel iff p | k (solutions form lines x + lambda j); (ii) a 0/1 vector with clause sums = 1 (mod p) has clause sums exactly 1 iff k <= p (sums lie in 0..k, next admissible value is 1+p). Hence 'S SAT iff Sol_p(S) contains a vector with <= 2 values' holds exactly for k = p: (3,3) and (5,5) yes; (4,2) no - GF(2) sees 'odd number true', not 'exactly one'; (3,2) no - j not in the kernel. GF(p)-blind MUS in the D-018 sense are defined only for k = p.
PREMISES: T44 C1 (D-018)
PROOF:
SOURCE: proofbook seq 1108; mission PNP-001/director; author model claude-opus-5-5; claim hash f822f11cb55f57c4; registered by pnp_autoreview

label: S0094
statement:
For positive 1-in-3, A x = 1 has an integer solution iff it is solvable modulo every power of 3 (3-adically); primes p != 3 never obstruct (x = j/3 is p-adically integral). Depth-1 Chvatal-Gomory refutation from the clause equalities is therefore exactly 3-adic linear algebra - polynomial time and strictly stronger than GF(3) from n=7 on. The arithmetic residual of 1-in-3 is {Boolean-UNSAT, Z-solvable}.

label: S0095
statement:

Solution counts mod 3 carry no information for positive 1-in-3; any useful count needs the j-direction quotiented out (count lines, i.e. 3^(d-1)).

PROOF:

label: S0106
statement:
D3 BASIS: B2 -> De Morgan for circuits: each XOR/XNOR gate becomes 3 De Morgan gates and both of its children acquire fan-out 2. A B2 circuit of size S with r reused gates and t parity gates becomes a De Morgan circuit of size <= 3S with <= r+2t reused gates. For FORMULAS the conversion is not polynomially size-preserving in the needed exponent (B2 shrinkage exponent is 1, parity), so CJW20-type bounds hold in the De Morgan basis; B2 results follow only through r+2t. CHOPRS20 almost-formulas are De Morgan, so frontier C is basis-consistent.
PREMISES: T07: every De Morgan circuit C of size S with r gates of fan-out > 1 has formula size L(C) <= 2^r (2S+1)

label: S0107
statement:
D4 REUSE-TO-CORRELATION DECOMPOSITION (exact): let C be a De Morgan circuit with gamma gates g_1..g_gamma of fan-out > 1 and S gates. For a in {0,1}^gamma let F_a(x) = AND_j [P_j(x,a) = a_j] AND P_out(x,a), where P_j, P_out are the principal formulas (CHOPRS20 Thm 30) with reused gates replaced by constants a. Then L(F_a) <= S+gamma, the F_a have pairwise disjoint supports and C = OR_a F_a. For any two distributions Y, Z: Pr_Y[C]-Pr_Z[C] = sum_a (Pr_Y[F_a]-Pr_Z[F_a]), so some formula F_a of size <= S+gamma has advantage >= Adv(C)/2^gamma. Reuse costs a factor 2^gamma in CORRELATION, not in size (T07 pays it in size).
PREMISES: CHOPRS20 Thm 30 proof (principal formulas)

label: S0109
statement:
D5 QUANTIFIER CHECK against OPS21: required is ONE fixed eps>0 that works for ALL sufficiently small beta>0, against general circuits. D2 meets the quantifier form (any fixed eps<1/2 for every beta) but only for De Morgan circuits with r <= (1+beta-2eps)log2 N reused gates. AF (if P1,P2 hold) meets it with gamma(beta) < N^{beta-eta} reused gates: as beta -> 0 this budget tends to N^{-eta}, while Circuit[N^{1+eps}] allows N^{1+eps} reused gates for every beta. Consequence: every PRG/correlation mechanism needs seed >= gamma, so it cannot cover circuits with gamma >= t = N^beta reused gates; for small beta the OPS21 hypothesis requires a mechanism that does not fool the circuit by a PRG of seed below its reuse count.
PREMISES: OPS21 (ToC v017a011, abstract-page theorem, numbering as Thm 1.4 unconfirmed): exists c>=1; if exists eps>0 such that for every small enough beta>0 Gap-MCSP[2^{beta n}/(cn), 2^{beta n}] notin Circuit[N^{1+eps}] then NP notsubset Circuit[poly] (hence P != NP); D2; AF
PROOF:

label: S0110
statement:
D6 REUSE COLLAPSE UNDER RESTRICTION (repair of the D5 limit): let d_g be the number of input variables gate g depends on. Under a truly random p-restriction, a reused gate stays a non-literal, non-constant reused gate only if >= 2 of its d_g variables stay live, so Pr <= C(d_g,2) p^2 <= p^2 d_g^2/2 (union over pairs) and E[gamma(C|rho)] <= sum_{g reused} min(1, p^2 d_g^2/2). With p = N^{beta+eps/5-1}: reused gates with d_g <= N^{1-beta-eta} contribute <= N^{-2 eta}, so only WIDE reused gates (d_g > N^{1-beta-eta}) can survive. Combined with AF: if P1, P2 hold, Gap-MCSP[N^beta] has no De Morgan circuit of size N^{1+eps} with at most N^{beta-2eta} wide reused gates (Markov over rho). Sanity check (dual-rail parity): the tree has ~N/2^j reused nodes with d_g = 2^j; sum_j (N/2^j) min(1,p^2 4^j) = Theta(pN) = Theta(k) survivors, matching counterexample 1 - those survivors are exactly the wide nodes (d_g >= 1/p). REMAINING OBLIGATION (unrestricted circuits): circuits computing Gap-MCSP[N^beta] with more than N^beta wide reused gates.
PREMISES: D4; AF; D5
PROOF:
SOURCE: proofbook seq 16770; mission director/closure; author model claude-opus-5-5; claim hash 9f883ddcca8b3ea7; registered by pnp_autoreview

statement:
A2 FAIL-FAST CONTROL FOR A: YES contains every table supported on any set T of m = N^beta/(c log N) positions (circuit size <= m log N). Hence |B_K^+| >= max_T |b_K(V_T)| for the coordinate subcubes V_T. Semantic compression therefore requires the reused-gate tuple b_K to take few values on EVERY sparse subcube - a property of the chosen cut gates, not of YES-instance sparsity. Combined with route B (YES side = PRG outputs G(z) o rho): |B^+_G| <= 2^{seed} while PRG error >= 2^{-seed}, so A o B gains only if the reused gates carry <= seed - O(log N) bits about the seed (same information threshold as D5).

statement:

Route G is the same obstacle (failures among simple inputs).

label: S0119
statement:
QO4 REASSESSMENT OF EXISTING LOWER BOUNDS BY THE RATIO eps(beta)/beta: of 368 cross-family-survived lower-bound steps (lb_audit, 602 total) none is a superlinear lower bound for general (unrestricted fan-in-2) circuits; all concern restricted classes (formulas, low reuse, streaming/update maps, restricted residual circuits). Formulas: CJW20 gives N^{2+beta-eps} (ratio unbounded) but only for De Morgan formulas. D2 in the Q2 regime (size N^{1+k beta}): De Morgan circuits with r <= (1-(k-1)beta-eps')log2 N reused gates are excluded for every k once beta < (1-eps')/(k-1) (T07 + CJW20-T5.5-GAP). D5's quantifier objection (fixed eps against a budget vanishing with beta) disappears under Q2, because the target exponent k beta vanishes too; the magnitude gap stays: AF covers <= N^{beta-eta} reused gates, a size-N^{1+k beta} circuit may have up to N^{1+k beta}. RESULT: no existing result satisfies Q2/Q3/Q*; the weakening changes the residual's size bound, not its type.

label: S0124
statement:
ST2 INDEPENDENT TRANSFER, STRENGTHENED (author Claude family; owner's sec. 9 argument with P = NP replaced by NP subset P/poly): let S be polylog-uniform AC0_d[2^{m^k}] with r CX rounds, uniformity time m^u. Bit i of X_j is a Sigma_{d'}-TIME[poly(m, L_j, log b)] predicate g_j(i, b, D_<j) with random access to the earlier answers D_<j (padding zeros beyond the description). Assume NP subset P/poly, so PH subset P/poly and Sigma_{d'} has circuits of size n^{c}. Induction: if every earlier answer has size <= m^{K_i}, hardwiring b and D_<j gives a circuit for X_j of size m^{K_j}, K_j = c*O(K_{j-1} + k + u), independent of b. For b > K* = max_j K_j the answer 'a circuit of size m^{K_j} for X_j' is admissible in every round (Teacher only has to exist, no uniformity needed), so X_r has circuit complexity <= m^{K*} < m^b at every large N: S fails for all b > K*. Hence: absolute protocol => NP notsubset P/poly (stronger than Thm 1.7's P != NP). Uses neither Lemma 5.4 nor SearchMCSP.

label: S0135
statement:
QO1 UPPER BOUND UNDER NP in P/poly (derivation of the OPS21 Thm 1.4 mechanism, author Claude family): NP subset SIZE[n^a] => there is K=K(a) such that for EVERY s=s(n) with n <= s <= 2^{n/2}: Gap-MCSP[s/(cn), s] on N=2^n bits has circuits of size N*s^K (a.e.). Proof: s'=s/(cn). Greedy anti-checker: V_0 = all circuits of size <= s', Y_0 = empty. Step i: for every position y in [N] (a fixed wire x_y) evaluate an approximate count of |{C in V_i: C(y) != x_y}|/|V_i| given (Y_i, x|Y_i, y, x_y) - input length L = O(t n), Stockmeyer approximate counting is in BPP^NP subset Sigma_3 subset P/poly (Karp-Lipton chain) so size L^{a'}; a tournament over the N candidates picks the best (y, x_y): N*L^{a'} gates per step. Elimination: if CC(x) > s then for every nonempty V_i some y kills >= 1/3 of V_i (minimax on V_i: otherwise a distribution over V_i is correct w.p. > 2/3 on every input and the majority of O(n) samples computes x with size O(n s') <= s, contradiction); with approximation >= 1/4. Hence V_t = empty after t = O(s' log s') steps. YES (CC(x) <= s'): the circuit for x is never eliminated. Final test 'V_t empty' is coNP on L bits. Total t*N*L^{a'} = N*s^{K}, K = a'+2, independent of s and beta. With s = N^beta: g_beta(N) <= N^{1+K beta} for all beta in (0,1/2]. c is the constant from the majority step (not necessarily 10).
PREMISES: OPS21 Thm 1.4 / Lemma 4.1 (anti-checker); CHOPRS20 Lemma 27; Stockmeyer approximate counting; Karp-Lipton: NP in P/poly => PH in P/poly

label: S0136
statement:
QO2 WEAKEST SUFFICIENT QUANTIFIER FORM Q*: if for every K >= 1 there is a size function s_K (n <= s_K <= 2^{n/2}) such that Gap-MCSP[s_K/(cn), s_K] has no circuits of size N*s_K^K for infinitely many n, then NP notsubset P/poly, hence P != NP (contrapositive of QO1). Special cases: Q1 (exists eps, all small beta: g_beta notin O(N^{1+eps})) => Q2 (for all k, delta exists beta < delta: g_beta notin O(N^{1+k beta}); take beta < min(delta, eps/k)) => Q* (s_K = N^beta). Q3 (fixed s = n^c, g notin O(N log^k N) for all k) => Q*. Lower bounds whose exponent ratio eps(beta)/beta is bounded (eps = beta, 2 beta) do NOT suffice since K is unknown; eps = sqrt(beta), beta log(1/beta) or N*(log N)^{omega(1)} at s = polylog do. label: S0144
statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (Corrected Reuse Collapse under Random Restriction): Let C be a De Morgan circuit of size |C| <= N^{1+eps} with a set of reused gates G_reused. For each g in G_reused let d_g be the number of input variables g depends on. Let p = N^{beta + eps/5 - 1} with beta > 0, eps >= 0. Under a random p-restriction rho, a reused gate g stays a non-literal, non-constant reused gate iff at least 2 of its d_g variables remain live. For any threshold D* = N^{(1-beta)/2 - eta - 7eps/10} with eta > 0, define W(C) = sum_{g in G_reused} min(1, p^2 d_g^2 / 2). Then E[gamma(C|rho)] <= W(C), where gamma(C|rho) is the number of surviving non-literal reused gates. If every reused gate has d_g <= D*, then W(C) <= (1/2) N^{beta - 2eta}. Consequently Pr[gamma(C|rho) > N^{beta - eta}] <= (1/2) N^{-eta} by Markov's inequality.
statement_end: Consequently Pr[gamma(C|rho) > N^{beta - eta}] <= (1/2) N^{-eta} by Markov's inequality.

structure.evidence: REPAIR of refuted D6 (S0110, S0113) and algebraically-flawed D6' (S0142). The threshold D* = N^{(1-beta)/2 - eta - 7eps/10} is derived by solving W(C) <= N^{beta-2eta}/2 for the exponent alpha where d_g <= N^alpha. With p = N^{beta+eps/5-1}, p^2 = N^{2beta+2eps/5-2}. For d_g <= D* = N^alpha, contribution per gate <= (1/2) N^{2alpha} N^{2beta+2eps/5-2}. With <= N^{1+eps} gates, total W(C) <= (1/2) N^{1+eps+2alpha+2beta+2eps/5-2} = (1/2) N^{2alpha+2beta+7eps/5-1}. Setting 2alpha+2beta+7eps/5-1 <= beta-2eta gives alpha <= (1-beta)/2 - 7eps/10 - eta. This D* is larger (weaker threshold) than the original D6's N^{1-beta-eta} because (1-beta)/2 < 1-beta for beta in (0,1). The residual class R' = {C: W(C) > N^{beta-2eta}} is therefore larger than the original R, making the surviving obligation harder but the lemma correct. No dependency on P1/P2; this is a pure counting bound.

label: S0145
statement:
EXCLUSION E-LEVIN (mechanism, not the statement): (a) for Levin's universal search U and every fixed algorithm A that outputs SAT witnesses, t_U(F) <= 2^{|A|} (t_A(F) + v(|F|)) with v the witness check time; hence 'U runs in polynomial time on all satisfiable F' <=> P = NP, and a lower bound for U is up to a constant factor a lower bound for every algorithm - the quantifier over algorithms is not removed. (b) Relative to an oracle A with P^A = NP^A (BGS, seq 3), U^A runs in polynomial time; every argument that uses U only through simulation and diagonalization relativizes and cannot show U superpolynomial. Excluded: pure simulation/diagonalization against U. Not excluded: arguments that use the Cook-Levin encoding of U's run non-black-box (short encodings of long computations); the only mechanism known to work there is the algorithmic method of Williams (succinct SAT), whose proven reach is NEXP/NQP lower bounds against ACC-type classes, not P != NP.

label: S0147
statement:
EXCLUSION E-PLS-BLACKBOX: (a) P = NP => PLS subset FP (prefix search for x with V(F(x)) <= V(x)); so 'some PLS problem has no polynomial-time algorithm' => P != NP, the converse is not known (the target is at least as strong as P != NP). Excluded: black-box-to-white-box transfer. Also: long improvement paths are not search hardness (binary counter: 2^m - 1 steps, end state 1...1 computable directly).

label: S0151
statement:
QUANTIFIER Q-WILLIAMS (owner 2026-11-26): 'for every k there is L_k in NP with L_k not in SIZE(n^k)' does not imply P != NP: by Kannan 1982, Sigma2 cap Pi2 is not in SIZE(n^k) for every fixed k; under P = NP, PH = P, so already P contains such an L_k for every k. Needed is the uniform-quantifier form 'EXISTS L in NP FORALL k: L not in SIZE(n^k)' (NP not in P/poly), or the uniform analogue for DTIME. Fixed-polynomial NP lower bounds and NQP lower bounds (Murray-Williams) are not approximations of P != NP.
PREMISES: Kannan 1982

label: S0153
statement:
T-NORM-F (refines seq 17140; CONDITIONAL on D4 seq 16760 and CORR-IK): the forest-size estimate s = p^2 N^{1+eps} is wrong in general. Tal's shrinkage E[L(F|rho)] = O(p^2 L log(1/p) + p sqrt(L)) applies per principal formula; with m principal formulas of sizes L_i (sum L_i = L <= N^{1+eps}, m up to N^{1+eps}), E[s] <= sum_i min(p L_i, O~(p^2 L_i + p sqrt(L_i))) <= O~(p^2 L + p sqrt(m L)), and circuits with all L_i = O(1) reach s ~ p L = N^{beta+6eps/5}. Worst case k^2/s >= p^2 N^2 / (2 p N^{1+eps}) = N^{beta-4eps/5}/2 (k = pN = N^{beta+eps/5}). Against D4's correlation >= 2^{-N^{beta-eta}} (w.p. >= 1 - N^{-eta} - 0.1 for gamma and s, Markov) the contradiction holds iff eta > 4eps/5 (+o(1)); with W budget N^{beta-2eta} >= 1 this needs 4eps/5 < eta < beta/2, i.e. eps < 5beta/8. The owner's conditions 1 - eps > beta - eta and beta + 6eps/5 < 1 used the formula-only size and are insufficient for general circuits.

label: S0155
statement:
SEED-FLOOR (proof of the D5 claim, seq 16768): if a distribution G on {0,1}^k has support size <= M (e.g. seed length l, M = 2^l), then some AND of t = floor(log2 M) + 1 <= k literals has |Pr_G - Pr_U| >= 2^{-t}: of the 2^t patterns on the first t coordinates at most M < 2^t are hit, a missed pattern has Pr_G = 0 and Pr_U = 2^{-t}. Hence fooling De Morgan formulas of size >= t with error delta forces log2 M >= log2(1/delta) - 1. In the D4/AF mechanism (error 2^{-r-2} for r surviving reused gates): seed >= r + 1, and since YES outputs G(z) o rho have circuit size <= N^beta, the support on the star coordinates is <= 2^{O(N^beta log N)}, so r <= O(N^beta log N). Consequence: every PRG instantiation of AF has polylog(1/delta)-exponent a >= 1 and covers at most N^{beta+o(1)} surviving reused gates; circuits with more surviving reuse must first be reduced by D6'/NORM.
PREMISES: seq 16760 (D4); seq 16762 (AF); seq 16768 (D5)
PROOF:

statement:

MECH-RANGE (parameter check against OPS21/Q2, seq 16795-16796): in AF with a PRG of seed s^{c+o(1)} (CKLM19: c = 1/3, seq 16757), stars >= N^{beta+eta/2} force p >= N^{beta+eta/2-1}; with the unconditional worst case s = p L, L = N^{1+eps} (D4-SIM), seed <= N^{beta-eta} needs c(beta + eta/2 + eps) <= beta - eta, so eps/beta < 1/c - 1 (c = 1/3: eps < 2beta). Hence eps(beta)/beta stays bounded for every fixed c and the mechanism cannot reach Q2 without a structural change. Two levers only: (i) c -> 0, a PRG for size-s De Morgan formulas with seed s^{o(1)}, which implies a function in E without polynomial-size De Morgan formulas (open, far beyond the known n^{3-o(1)}); (ii) a bound on the number m of principal formulas: with a Tal-type forest bound (P2) s <~ p^2 L + p sqrt(m L), Q2 requires m <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta} at total size N^{1+eps} with eps/beta -> infinity. The 'fundamental change' asked for by the owner is therefore a reduction of m (count of reused gates), not of W; this is a necessary condition, not a construction.

label: S0161
statement:
MMW-UNFOLD (cost of the K1/MMW route, Q-5d167697b4; MMW19 Lemma 3.1 as verified in seq 10407: size O~(N s/l), depth O(log N / log l), Circuit-Min-Merge[s] gates with l-bit input, l >= s^2; tree with fan-out 1, seq 9992): replacing every gate by a De Morgan formula of size l^b and unfolding, each input bit of a gate is read up to l^{b-1} times on average, so the child subformula is copied that often per level; over depth log N/log l the total formula size is about N^{b+O(beta)}. A contradiction with CJW20 (N^{2+beta-xi}) therefore needs b < 2 - Theta(beta): the GATE function Circuit-Min-Merge[s] on l = N^{2beta} bits must have SUBQUADRATIC formulas. NP subset P/poly gives the gates circuits of size l^a and no formula bound at all (even NP subset Formula[poly] gives only some fixed b, not b < 2). Hence the middle formula L(C_MMW) <= N^{2-delta} s^K is the R-MCSP-type obligation for an MCSP-like function at scale l (self-similar), not a weaker obligation. Open as before; it does not bypass R-MCSP.

label: S0163
statement:
MMW-M (CLAIMED; owner question 2026-11-26: does the MMW Merge architecture give the MECH-RANGE bound m <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta}?): in MMW19 Lemma 3.1 circuits the top tree has fan-out 1 (seq 9992), so every reused gate is (a) an output bit of a non-root Circuit-Min-Merge gate read more than once by the parent gate's replacement, or (b) a reused gate inside a replacement. There are >= N/l non-root gates (l-bit inputs cover N truth-table bits) with ~ s log s output bits each. MECH-RANGE then requires (a) l >= N^{eps-3beta+7eta} unless most description bits are read once by the parent, and (b) total reuse inside all replacements <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta}, i.e. per gate <= l N^{4beta-eps+o(1)}: for eps/beta -> infinity the gate function Circuit-Min-Merge[s] on l = N^{Omega(eps)} bits must be computed by near-formulas whose reuse is sublinear in l by a factor N^{-(eps-4beta)}. NP subset P/poly supplies arbitrary circuits for the gates and no such structure. So the architecture moves the whole m-bound into the gate function: the same reuse obligation (R-MCSP type) at scale l, as in MMW-UNFOLD (seq 17162). This is a NECESSARY condition derived from the architecture, not a proof that suitable gate circuits do not exist.

label: S0166
statement:
FOURIER-SUP (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check line by line; CLAIMED until cross-family review). Let E be any encoding of x in {0,1}^N from which D_x(C)=d_H(x,tt(C)) is recoverable within additive error tau for every C in C_a, a >= c m. Parities C_u(i)=u.i mod 2 have size O(m), so they are in C_a. For booleans (c xor x)-(c xor y)=(x-y)(-1)^c, hence D_x(C_u)-D_y(C_u)=sum_i (x_i-y_i)(-1)^{u.i}. E(x)=E(y) forces each such value into [-2tau,2tau]; Parseval gives N d_H(x,y)=sum_u(...)^2 <= N 4tau^2, so d_H(x,y) <= 4tau^2. Each E-class lies in a Hamming ball of radius 4tau^2=O(N^{2beta}/m^2)=o(N) for beta<1/2, so |E| >= N - O(tau^2 log N) bits; the same holds at every dyadic node interval I with |I| >> tau^2. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): any uniform (sup over C_a) approximation of the full error landscape D, linear or not, regardless of decoding time.

label: S0167
statement:
CJ3-R (REPAIR of seq 16802 / Q-88090df9cf:S0139; owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Input x then y (n bits each), n known. m=ceil(log2(2n+2)), h=floor(log2 m), budget B=m^{max(1,floor(sqrt h))}. A* runs all programs of description length <= h (K <= 2m) as bit generators P(n,i), each cut off after B simulated steps; per program an active bit and a bit d_P. Every stream bit is compared with P(n,i) (mismatch or timeout deactivates); in the second half A* recomputes P(n,i) for x_i from the program instead of re-reading it and sets d_P |= P(n,i) AND y_i. Output: NOT d_P for an active program, else a fixed default b0. ONE PASS, no random access (objection 3 fixed); m(n) and the time bound are explicit (objections 1, 2 fixed). Correctness: a program still active at the end reproduced every input bit, so d_P = [x and y intersect]. T = n m^{O(sqrt log m)}, S = m^{O(sqrt log m)}, inside the CJSW class for f(n)=ceil(log2 log2(n+2)) (any f=omega(sqrt log log n)). Every fixed deterministic generator with (log n)^c time per bit is enumerated and within budget for all large n, so A* answers correctly on its outputs. COLLISIONS: if u != v are prefixes produced by such generators, the generator of u is active after u and inactive after v, so A*'s states differ (for all large n): deterministic polylog-time collision generators are EXCLUDED against A* (unconditional). Under P=NP the PH collapses on input length m=log n, so every polylogtime-uniform AC0 generator (single bit in PH on m) is computed in time m^{O(1)}=(log n)^{O(1)} and is also captured.
PREMISES: seq 16802 (CJ3); CJSW Thm 1.4 (theoretics.episciences.org)

CJ3-R (REPAIR of seq 16802 / Q-88090df9cf:S0139; owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Input x then y (n bits each), n known. m=ceil(log2(2n+2)), h=floor(log2 m), budget B=m^{max(1,floor(sqrt h))}. A* runs all programs of description length <= h (K <= 2m) as bit generators P(n,i), each cut off after B simulated steps; per program an active bit and a bit d_P. Every stream bit is compared with P(n,i) (mismatch or timeout deactivates); in the second half A* recomputes P(n,i) for x_i from the program instead of re-reading it and sets d_P |= P(n,i) AND y_i. Output: NOT d_P for an active program, else a fixed default b0. ONE PASS, no random access (objection 3 fixed); m(n) and the time bound are explicit (objections 1, 2 fixed). Correctness: a program still active at the end reproduced every input bit, so d_P = [x and y intersect]. T = n m^{O(sqrt log m)}, S = m^{O(sqrt log m)}, inside the CJSW class for f(n)=ceil(log2 log2(n+2)) (any f=omega(sqrt log log n)). Every fixed deterministic generator with (log n)^c time per bit is enumerated and within budget for all large n, so A* answers correctly on its outputs. COLLISIONS: if u != v are prefixes produced by such generators, the generator of u is active after u and inactive after v, so A*'s states differ (for all large n): deterministic polylog-time collision generators are EXCLUDED against A* (unconditional). Under P=NP the PH collapses on input length m=log n, so every polylogtime-uniform AC0 generator (single bit in PH on m) is computed in time m^{O(1)}=(log n)^{O(1)} and is also captured.

label: S0168
statement:
A*-REFUTER (owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). u_j = 1-P_j(n,j) if P_j answers within B, else 0 (j <= K); u_{K+1}=1; other bits 0; v = 0^n if b0=0, v = e_{K+1} if b0=1. Every P_j mismatches at position j, so A* outputs b0, while DISJ(u,v)=1-b0: R refutes A* at every large n without simulating A*'s stream. L_R={<n,i>: R(1^n)_i=1} is in DTIME(m^{O(sqrt log m)}); L_R is NOT in P (unconditional): a fixed m^c-time program for L_R would be enumerated and kept active, so A* would be correct on R(1^n) - this is a time-hierarchy diagonal, nothing beyond the hierarchy theorem. CC(R(1^n)) = O(m^2) (at most 2m+2 ones: DNF of minterms), so R is non-uniformly easy; the sparse algorithm A** (store the <= K+1 one-positions of x, O(m^2) space, check them against y) solves every R-instance unconditionally. So R refutes A* only, not the class; CJSW's search-MCSP algorithm (P=NP) would also capture it.
PREMISES: CJ3-R

label: S0169
statement:
A*-STRENGTH (director, 2026-11-26; CLAIMED). (i) The open step 'L_R in PH' implies P != NP at once (L_R in PH minus P gives PH != P); A* is only the device certifying L_R not in P. More generally any refuter R* of A* (infinitely often) whose bit function is in PH gives a PH language outside P: the route is at least as strong as P != NP, not a reduction of it. (ii) L_R is hard for DTIME(m^{sqrt(log m)/2}) under polynomial-time reductions: for M deciding L' in that time, encode w in the m-bit number n_w and take the fixed program Q='decode w from n, run M(w)' of constant rank j0; then w in L' iff <n_w,j0> not in L_R. Hence L_R in PH iff (up to the constant in the exponent) DTIME(m^{Theta(sqrt log m)}) is contained in PH - a superpolynomial-time inclusion strictly stronger than P != NP. Relative to a PSPACE-complete oracle A, PH^A = P^A while the relativized time hierarchy keeps DTIME^A(m^{sqrt log m}) outside P^A, so the open step is false relative to A: any proof must be non-relativizing. (iii) Corrections to the 2026-11-26 review note: 'P=NP gives only polynomial, not polylogarithmic time' is wrong, since poly(m) = polylog(n); the refuter need not simulate A* over the stream (A*-REFUTER).
PREMISES: A*-REFUTER; CJ3-R
PROOF:

CJW20-GAP (owner derivation 2026-11-26 from the proof, director check against local copy eccc-TR20-065 paper.txt l.1216-1280; CLAIMED, a corollary of the PROOF, not the stated theorem). The proof of Thm 5.5 only uses: F accepts G(z) o rho (circuit size <= s'^{1/3+o(1)} + polylog, s' = restricted formula size) and rejects a random completion of rho (size >= k/(10 log k), k = |rho^{-1}(*)| >= pn/2). These are independent knobs: choose p so that k/(10 log k) > b, then L <= a^{3-o(1)} n^2/(k^2 n^{o(1)}) keeps the YES side <= a. All losses (shrinkage n^{C/loglog n}, PRG o(1), polylog for rho) go into the exponent, not into the gap. Hence for fixed beta in (0,1) and xi > 0: Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(10 log N), N^beta] has no probabilistic De Morgan formulas of size N^{2+beta-xi} for large N. TRUNCATED VERSION (owner count, checked): YES = some a-circuit with distance 0; NO = every a-circuit at distance > tau, a = N^beta/(10 log N), tau = Theta(N^beta/log N). The CJW YES distribution is exact; for the random completion of k = N^{beta+xi/5} free bits, Pr[some a-circuit within tau] <= 2^{O(a log a)} V(k,tau) 2^{-k} = 2^{-N^{beta+xi/5}+O(N^beta)}. Same bound N^{2+beta-xi}. CHOPRS Lemma 22 is not needed (owner: it assumes QP in P/poly and uses XOR encodings; not checked locally). This is a FORMULA bound; QO2 still asks for general circuits.

statement:

Truncated D^(tau)=min(tau,D) composes exactly; node state BOT or (C_I,E_I), |E_I| < tau, O(N^beta) bits, lossless for x_I and itself a circuit of size <= b; the tree is an MMW tree with tau-tolerant merge gates; FOURIER-SUP does not apply (far tables all map to BOT). label: S0173
statement:
ROBUST-GAMMA (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED, corollary of the CJW20 Thm 5.5 proof). a = N^beta/(10 log N), tau = N^gamma, 0 < beta < gamma < 1. Promise: YES = some a-circuit at distance 0, NO = every a-circuit at distance > tau. Restriction with k >= N^{gamma+o(1)} free bits (p = N^{gamma-1+o(1)}): Pr[some a-circuit within tau] <= 2^{O(N^beta)} 2^{tau log(ek/tau)} 2^{-k} = 2^{-Omega(k)}; restricted size p^2 L N^{o(1)}, CKLM PRG outputs have size L_rest^{1/3+o(1)} <= a iff L <= N^{2+3beta-2gamma-xi}. So the promise problem has no probabilistic De Morgan formulas of size N^{2+3beta-2gamma-xi}. SAMPLING (checked): t = O(N^{1+beta-gamma}) uniform positions J; NO: each a-circuit survives with prob <= e^{-t tau/N}, union over 2^{O(N^beta)} circuits; YES always accepted. So a uniform bound L(H_{J,a}) <= L_H for the partial-consistency predicate H_{J,a} gives probabilistic formulas of size L_H (J hard-wired). In t: N^{2+3beta-2gamma} = t^{2+beta/u}, u = 1+beta-gamma, which is CJW20's exponent 2+theta for MCSP[t^theta] with theta = beta/u (consistency check: no new strength).

statement:

For EVERY set J of t = Theta(N^u) distinct positions, u = 1+beta-gamma, a = N^beta/(10 log N): H_{J,a}(z) = [some a-circuit C has C(j_r) = z_r for all r] has no probabilistic De Morgan formulas of size N^{2u+beta-xi} = t^{2+beta/u-o(1)}. label: S0175
statement:
DECOUPLE-ACCOUNTING2 (replaces seq 17208; director, owner check 2026-11-26; CLAIMED). (i) QO1 (seq 16795) gives circuits N*s^K for GAP-MCSP[s/(cn), s]; its anti-checker step needs the gap. label: S0177
statement:
NONADAPT-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; part of CONV-D seq 17216). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), m = log2 N, dyadic blocks of size B = Theta(b m) with a large constant. Counting gives y in {0,1}^B with CC(y) > b; x^(I) = y on block I, 0 elsewhere, has CC(x^(I)) >= CC(y) > b (restriction), so every x^(I) is a Gap-MCSP[a,b] NO instance. If a sample J sees <= r = Theta(a/m) positions of I, one equality test of O(m) gates per observed one gives an a-circuit consistent with x^(I) on J, so the partial-consistency test accepts. E_I|J n I| = tB/N, Markov: Pr_I[|J n I| > r] <= tB/(N r) = O(t m^3/N); for J random but independent of the input, averaging gives a fixed NO instance rejected with probability O(t m^3/N). Hence t = Omega(N/(log N)^3) for constant rejection. Director extensions: (i) the bound holds for EVERY non-adaptive tester with perfect completeness (any view consistent with a YES table must be accepted), not only for the consistency rule; (ii) ADAPTIVE one-sided testers: on x^(I) the run equals the run on 0^N (a YES instance) until a query hits I, so t = Omega(N/B) = Omega(N^{1-beta}/log N). Scope: excludes sublinear single-sample consistency for plain Gap-MCSP (consistent with the closed sampling route: tau = Theta(b/m) there needs t = Theta(N m)); does NOT constrain input-dependent anti-checkers or families of anti-checkers (an AND over a family needs total sample size >= N/polylog, below the trivial formula size N).

label: S0178
statement:
ADAPT-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; strengthens NONADAPT-LB seq 17222). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), beta fixed. (i) Small YES circuits: split the m index bits into q = O(1/beta) groups of beta m/2 bits, decode every group completely (O_beta(N^{beta/2}) = o(a) gates); each one-position is then an AND of q decoded lines, so ANY set of r = a/(2q) = Theta_beta(b/m) ones has an a-circuit (previously r = Theta(a/m)). (ii) A uniform table with exactly R = C_beta b ones is a NO instance with prob 1-o(1): C(N,R) = 2^{Omega(R log(N/R))} against 2^{O(b log(b+m))} circuits. (iii) A one-sided algorithm (YES always accepted) cannot reject while it has seen <= r ones, since the table with exactly the observed ones is a YES instance consistent with every answer. Each new adaptive query hits a one with prob <= R/(N-t), so E X_t <= tR/(N-t) and Pr[reject] <= Pr[X_t > r] <= O_beta(t m/N); averaging over the NO-heavy distribution gives a fixed NO instance, so t = Omega_beta(N/log N) for adaptive and non-adaptive one-sided algorithms. Director scope note: CJW20 and CONV-D allow TWO-SIDED error; for two-sided algorithms the same distributions (YES: uniform r-subset, NO: uniform R-subset) give only t = Omega(N/R) = Omega_beta(N^{1-beta}) (views are all-zero with prob >= 1 - tR/N under both). Query bounds of order N/polylog do not constrain CONV-D, whose formulas have size >= N anyway; they exclude only bit-selection (sampling) as the conversion mechanism.
PREMISES: NONADAPT-LB seq 17222; CONV-D seq 17216

label: S0179
statement:
AC-FAMILY-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; novelty vs. literature not confirmed - CHOPRS Cor 61 refutes the OPS Anti-Checker Hypothesis by a different route). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), constants beta, zeta > 0. Let J_1..J_l be a FIXED (input-independent) family with |J_i| <= N^{1-zeta}. Uniform table with exactly R = D b ones (NO w.p. 1-o(1), as in ADAPT-LB seq 17227). By ADAPT-LB (i) any r = Theta_beta(b/m) ones have an a-circuit, so J_i is an anti-checker only if X_i = |J_i n ones| >= r. Hypergeometric tail: Pr[X_i >= r] <= (e|J_i|R/(N r))^r = (O_beta(m N^{-zeta}))^r = 2^{-Omega_{beta,zeta}(b)}. Union bound: for l <= 2^{c b} (c small) some NO instance has no anti-checker in the family. So a fixed family needs l >= 2^{Omega_{beta,zeta}(N^beta)} members. Any rule using only the family's consistency bits sees on that NO instance exactly what it sees on 0^N (a YES instance), so it accepts; an AND-of-tests formula over such a family has >= l leaves. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): fixed families of sublinear anti-checker candidates, any polynomial (even 2^{c N^beta}) size. NOT excluded: input-dependent anti-checkers; sets of size N^{1-o(1)}. CORRECTION of the scope note in seq 17222 ('does NOT constrain families'): fixed families are constrained by this count.

label: S0180
statement:
WEIGHTED-SUBST (owner bound 2026-11-26, director check and split; CLAIMED; within CONV-D seq 17216). F(x) = V(A(x)), A = anti-checker generator outputting t labelled positions (y_i, x_{y_i}), V = consistency predicate on T = t(m+1) bits. Substituting a formula for each output bit A_j at each of its mu_j(V) occurrences gives exactly L(F) <= sum_j mu_j(V) L(A_j); sum_j mu_j(V) = L(V). Director split, with t = N^{K beta}: (R1) L(V) <= N^{2+beta-Delta} is needed; V is an NP predicate on T = N^{O(beta)} bits, so ANY fixed polynomial bound L(V) <= T^C (C independent of beta) suffices for small beta - but NP subset P/poly gives V only circuits; R1 is 'V in Formula[poly]', supplied by NP subset Formula[poly] (OPS's stronger hypothesis), not by NP subset P/poly. Lower bound for R1: fixing the position inputs restricts V to H_{J,a}, so by PARTIAL-MCSP-LB seq 17211 (u = K beta) L(V) >= t^{2+1/K-o(1)}, and V has >= t^{2+1/K-o(1)} value-bit leaves - polynomial, consistent with R1. (R2) Given R1, max_j L(A_j) <= N^{2+beta-Delta-CK beta} suffices: every anti-checker output bit needs a SUBQUADRATIC formula; the weights mu_j matter only up to the factor L(V) = N^{O(beta)}. Unconditional counterpart (CJW20-GAP seq 17198): for every anti-checker generator with L(V) <= T^C, some output bit has L(A_j) >= N^{2+beta-xi-CK beta}; deriving the opposite from the assumption is the obligation. OPS 2021 p.23 (local copy toc-v017a011 l.1168-1172) names exactly R2 (rounds re-inspect earlier y_j) as the obstacle under NP subset Formula[poly].

label: S0181
statement:
FACTOR-WITNESS (director, 2026-11-26, answering the owner's T07-S0290 synthesis question; CLAIMED). Split the table into k aligned blocks x_1..x_k. Product factorisation (AND over blocks of [x_i has an a'-circuit]) or score folding (sum_i min_{C_i} D_i(C_i)) replaces the SHARED witness (exists C forall i) by independent witnesses (forall i exists C_i). Facts: CC(x_i) <= CC(x)+O(m) and CC(x) <= sum_i CC(x_i) + O(km). (i) VALID for Gap-MCSP[a,b], b = 10ma, when k <= c1 m: YES gives every block <= a+O(m) =: a'; NO gives some block > (b-O(km))/k > a'. (ii) INVALID for k >= c2 m: let block i be the table of an independent random circuit of size a/2; every block test accepts (CC <= a/2 < a', every D*_i = 0), while there are 2^{k Omega(a log a)} such tables and circuits of size S number 2^{O(S log S)}, so some such x has CC(x) >= Omega(k a) > b. The window is Theta(log N) components, tight up to constants. (iii) In the valid window the factorised formula is a sum of k Gap-MCSP formulas on N/k bits with constant gap, covered by CJW20-GAP (the proof's knobs are independent of the gap factor): exponent unchanged (BLOCK-EMB seq 17180, ratio invariance). MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): component factorisation / score folding with independent per-component witnesses as an exponent-gaining conversion, for any number of components. Consequence for T07 (seq 16758, A1 semantic T07 seq 16774) + S0290: the enumeration over cut assignments can be factorised only where the coupling through the shared witness is removed, which is (i)-(ii); a remaining route needs a compression of the shared-witness coupling that is not a product over components. Not located in the current registry: the CAPP steps S0258/S0290 (other question state); their full proofs were not re-read here.

statement:
SEP-MERGE-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director checked; CLAIMED). Gap-MCSP[a,b], b = N^beta, a = b/(10m). Split the table into q equal dyadic blocks. Any realisation F = OR_{sigma in {0,1}^w} AND_{j<=q} F_{j,sigma}(x_j) (arbitrary local F_{j,sigma}) needs w >= B/2 = Omega_beta(N^beta) for q = C_beta m. Proof checked: B = Theta(a log a) a power of 2 with every B-bit table of circuit size <= a (Lupanov); the periodic tables y^{N/B} are 2^B YES instances (the circuit reads only the low log B index bits); blocks are dyadic of size >= B, so each block contains whole periods and distinct y give distinct block restrictions; a sigma accepting k patterns accepts their k^q block-wise mixtures (product of the A_{j,sigma}), none of which may be a NO instance, and at most 2^{O(b log b)} tables have CC <= b, so k <= 2^{O(b log b / q)} <= 2^{B/2} for q = C_beta m; hence 2^w >= 2^{B/2}. Tight up to a log factor: sigma = a size-b circuit description (O(b log b) bits) with F_{j,sigma}(x_j) = [x_j = block j of tt(sigma)] is a valid realisation, so w = Theta~_beta(N^beta). Type: nondeterministic q-party number-in-hand cover / fooling-set bound; novelty not checked. SCOPE: (1) block-faithful: after fixing sigma no condition reads two blocks; the recursive elimination of SEP-ELIM-LB flattens by distributivity to this form with w <= (#leaves) W_path, so with leaves = blocks W_path >= Omega_beta(N^beta / log N). (2) NOT a formula lower bound: formula size corresponds to Karchmer-Wigderson games (seq 3616), not to rectangle covers; the owner's equality example (cover 2^B, formula O(qB)) shows the gap. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): block-faithful separator / conditional-state enumeration, including a conditional S0290-style score convolution over shared variables in the OR_sigma AND_j form, as an exponent-gaining conversion for Gap-MCSP.

label: S0185
statement:
GRID-DEG check (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting: H_{G,q}(X) = OR_alpha AND_v X_{v,alpha|E(v)} on the r x r grid, d = r^2 groups; P = arithmetisation (GF(2) or Z) of a Boolean circuit of size S for H, deg P <= d+k. (1) TRANSFER CORRECT as a formal identity: the inclusion-exclusion P* keeps monomials touching every group; prod_v Q_v = sum_{|U|<=k} prod_{v in U} D_v on such monomials (D_v kills monomials of degree 1 in group v, at most k groups are heavy); prod_v Q_v also performs x^2 -> x inside each group and kills two-variable products, so prod_v Q_v(P*) is the exactly-one-variable-per-group part of the multilinearisation ML(H); in ML(H) = sum over nonempty sets A of alphas of +-prod(union of monomials) only singletons A give one variable per group (two distinct alpha differ at some vertex), so the result is Z_{G,q} with all coefficients 1 in any characteristic. Size (S+1) 2^d binom(d,k) q^{O(k)}. (2) THE HYPOTHESIS NEVER HOLDS - every P agreeing with H on {0,1}^n has deg P >= deg_F(H) (multilinearisation does not raise degree); setting all variables of every vertex except one interior vertex v0 to 1 turns H into OR of the q^4 variables of v0, whose degree is q^4 over every field; hence deg P >= q^4 and k >= q^4 - r^2 for EVERY circuit, of every size. The derived k = Omega((log q)^{1/12}) is implied by this trivial bound and carries no information about S. VERDICT: GRID-DEG is a true but vacuous unconditional statement; no gap shrinks. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): transfer from arithmetic state-sum lower bounds to Boolean circuits via the total degree (or degree excess) of the arithmetised Boolean circuit - for any Boolean function of high F-degree every representation has high degree, independently of circuit size. The verdict does not depend on the cited arithmetic lower bound. Route closed, statement not refuted.
PREMISES: owner GRID-DEG 2026-11-26

label: S0187
statement:
CHMY-SEED-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; owner task 'improve the CHMY/Forbes-Kelley generator'; CLAIMED). Inputs: CHMY (ECCC TR20-103, local literature/sources/eccc-TR20-103) Lemma 19 (l.718: q-state time-t one-tape DTM = sum over alpha in A of ROBPs P_alpha of width exp(O(sqrt t log tq)), |A| <= (tq)^{O(sqrt t)}), Corollary 39 / Theorem 20 (generic ROBP PRG with error eps' = eps/|A|), Theorem 47 (needs MCSP[2^{mu n}] not in DTIME1[N^{1.01}] for a SMALL mu > 0), Corollary 17 (l.657, unconditional: MCSP[s] in DTIME1^O[N poly(s)] for some O in Sigma3^P, queries of length poly(s)), Lemma 21 (oracle queries of length l and fixed coins folded into q 2^l t states); SEED-FLOOR seq 17150 (support M => some AND of floor(log2 M)+1 literals has error >= 2^{-t}). (a) LEMMA: every distribution whose samples all have CC <= s and which eps'-fools all n-input ROBPs of width >= 2 satisfies s log s >= Omega(log(1/eps')). Proof: support <= #circuits of size s = 2^{O(s log s)}; an AND of literals is a width-2 ROBP; apply SEED-FLOOR. (b) In the CHMY architecture eps' = eps/|A| = eps (tq)^{-Theta(sqrt t)}, hence s >= Omega~(sqrt t log(tq)). For t = N^{1.01}, q = O(1): s >= N^{0.505-o(1)}, i.e. mu >= 0.505 - o(1), while Theorem 47 needs mu below the small constant of MMW. Forbes-Kelley (Theorem 38: seed O~(log(nw/eps')) log^3 n = O~(sqrt t log tq)) is already optimal in this architecture up to polylog factors. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): improving the generator recursion G_{i+1} = D_i xor (T_i and G_i), or any generic ROBP PRG, inside the Lemma-19 union-bound architecture, as a route to small mu. (c) Further unconditional constraint from Corollary 17 + Lemma 21 (deterministic Sigma3 oracle machine, no coins): no distribution on strings of CC <= s fools all (2^{poly(s)})-state DTMs of time N poly(s) (the folded Corollary-17 machine accepts all of them and rejects almost all uniform strings). Hence any improved generator for small mu must have a guarantee that FAILS at q = 2^{poly(s)} states, i.e. it must use that the attacked machine has few states. SURVIVING constructive directions (not lanes, recorded for the owner task): (i) a decomposition of time-N^{1.01} one-tape DTMs into <= 2^{N^{mu}} pieces (replacing Lemma 19's (tq)^{sqrt t} crossing-sequence guesses), or (ii) an analysis that fools the specific machine without the union bound over A (cancellations among P_alpha), in both cases exploiting q = O(1).
PREMISES: CHMY Lemma 19, Cor 17, Lemma 21, Thm 38/39, Thm 47 (TR20-103); SEED-FLOOR seq 17150

statement:
JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; extends CHMY-SEED-FLOOR seq 17279 to the owner's proposal 'control the error of the whole state distribution jointly instead of per branching program'; CLAIMED). (2) FLOOR for every analysis that uses only the decomposition M = OR_{alpha in A} P_alpha with each P_alpha a read-once BP of width <= w (any fixed order per alpha) and Pr_U[M=1] <= gamma: let H be the image of G (all CC <= s, so |H| <= 2^{O(s log s)} and |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma). A width-w ROBP in any fixed order accepts any prescribed set of <= w strings (one path per string, <= w distinct prefixes per level), so H is the union of ceil(|H|/w) such ROBPs; if ceil(|H|/w) <= |A| this OR is a member of the class, has acceptance measure |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma, and accepts all of H. statement:
BIAS-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; check of the owner's global Fourier error balance for the Forbes-Kelley step; CLAIMED). Owner's identities verified: (i) Parseval + Cauchy-Schwarz: sum_S |f^(S)| <= sqrt(A) for f in {0,1} with A accepted inputs; (ii) for independent D_i, T_i, G_i: b_{D xor (T and G)}(S) = b_D(S) E_T b_G(S cap T), so |b_{G_{i+1}}(S)| <= delta_i and Delta <= delta_i sqrt(A); (iii) signed S0290 convolution f^(S) = 2^{-N} sum_{u_1+..+u_q >= T} prod_j D_{j,S}(u_j) for disjoint components (Walsh characters are multiplicative over the components). LEMMA (unconditional): for every F subset {0,1}^N with |F| = A and every distribution Y supported in F, max_{S nonempty} |b_Y(S)| >= (1 - A 2^{-N}) / sqrt(A). Proof: apply (i) to f = 1_F: 1 - A 2^{-N} = E f(Y) - E f(U) = sum_{S nonempty} f^(S) b_Y(S) <= max|b_Y| sqrt(A). CONSEQUENCE: with F = {CC <= s}, A <= 2^{O(s log s)}, the bias delta < 1/(6 sqrt A) required by the owner's balance cannot be achieved by ANY distribution whose outputs all have CC <= s; a generator that meets it necessarily has outputs of CC > s. Source: literature/sources/anthropic-eth (paper dated Oct 26, 2026; Lean v4.33.1); the follow-up optimality analysis (Hexagon 2610.00692, 31 Oct 2026) is NOT local and not checked. (1) delta_ad delta_bc = delta_ac delta_bd - eps_ab eps_cd with eps = [[0,1],[-1,0]] (owner) is the same identity as [x=v][y=u] = [x=u][y=v] - phi(x,y)phi(u,v) (phi(0,1) = 1 = eps_01, phi(1,0) = -1 = eps_10), verified on all 16 points; lambda = 1 (two-square) case of Section 2.5. (2) STRUCTURE (unchanged): Lemma 19's sum and the space x time tableau of a one-tape DTM are path / planar networks without crossing constraints; the identity acts only on crossings, which have to be created by a re-embedding first; the CHMY cost is the bond dimension exp(Theta(sqrt t log tq)) of the path, not a crossing cost. (3) SIGNED ERROR SPLIT Delta = Delta_1 - Delta_2: any analysis that bounds Delta_1 and Delta_2 for generic width-w ROBP terms (K terms) is covered by JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR seq 17284 (1_H is such a sum with coefficients 1) and needs log(wK) <= N^{mu+o(1)}; a gain needs a cancellation between Delta_1 and Delta_2 that depends on M's resources (seq 17286: a bound that only uses the number of accepted inputs is impossible). VERDICT unchanged: no transfer at the needed strength is visible; statement not refuted. A combination with Weg 2 must exhibit (a) a representation of an O(1)-state time-N^{1.01} one-tape DTM with crossings whose rewriting lowers the bond dimension from exp(sqrt t) to exp(N^{o(1)}), and (b) a non-generic cancellation estimate for the signed terms.

label: S0191
statement:
CROSS-CHMY check (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Sign: delta_ad delta_bc = delta_ac delta_bd - eps_ab eps_cd with eps_01 = 1, eps_10 = -1 is exactly the identity recorded in seq 17297 (1) (minus sign, verified on 16 points); no correction needed. (1) Embedding Delta = sum_alpha sum_x W(x) P_alpha(x), W = Pr_G - 2^{-N}: correct by linearity, over Q. (2) Unfolded-circuit tensor network M(x) = sum_z [z_out = 1] prod_g [z_g = g(z_in(g))]: correct (unique consistent assignment), standard circuit-to-tensor-network embedding; for a one-tape DTM the unfolded network is the space x time tableau, a planar local network, so it still contains no crossings for the identity of seq 17297 to act on (seq 17297 (2) unchanged). (3) Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz |Delta|^2 <= p chi^2, chi^2 = sum_{p_alpha>0} (g_alpha - p_alpha)^2 / p_alpha (p_alpha = 0 forces g_alpha = 0 since P_alpha then accepts nothing): correct, BUT DOMINATED: by the same Cauchy-Schwarz, sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| <= sqrt(p chi^2), so |Delta| <= sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| <= sqrt(p chi^2); the weighted balance is never stronger than the triangle inequality, which itself contains no factor |A|. In CHMY |A| enters only through the UNIFORM per-term error eps' = eps/|A| (Cor 39), not through the triangle inequality; the weighted form removes nothing. (4) LOGICAL STRENGTH of CROSS-RES (chi^2 < 1/(36p)): it implies sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| < 1/6, the old obligation, so it is at least as hard; term-generic bounds are covered by JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR seq 17284. If M is a correct MCSP[s] algorithm and G is supported in {CC <= s}, then Delta = 1 - p and chi^2 >= (1-p)^2/p > 1/(36p); so CROSS-RES for such G is equivalent to M not being a correct MCSP algorithm - a reformulation of the lower bound, not a reduction. STATUS: CROSS-ID, embedding and the weighted inequality are correct and standard; they do not shrink the gap. The open step remains a non-uniform, resource-using per-term error estimate (seq 17279, 17284, 17286, 17297).

label: S0192
statement:
SHIFT-LEMMA19 (owner derivation 2026-11-26 from Viola's proof behind CHMY Lemma 19, director check; CLAIMED; model DTIME1: one-way read-only input tape, two-way work tape, CHMY l.146). Checked: (1) each work-head move crosses exactly one boundary of exactly one shift class d, so sum_d C_d(x) <= t, E_d C_d <= t/B, Pr_d[C_d > R] <= eta for R = ceil(t/(B eta)). (2) For fixed d a crossing record alpha (time-ordered, all boundaries) with l <= R entries (direction, state with current input symbol, input position) determines the block index (start block from d, then +-1 per crossing); input positions are non-decreasing, so K <= sum_{l<=R} (2q')^l binom(N+l, l), log K = O(R log(2q'(1+N/R))). (3) P_{d,alpha} simulates the block visits block by block, reading the input intervals in the order given by alpha (unknown-order read-once), storing one block (B cells), the state and a pointer into alpha: log w = O(B + log t). (4) F = (1/B) sum_d sum_{|alpha|<=R} P_{d,alpha}; determinism gives at most one consistent accepting alpha per d, so F = M Pr_d[C_d <= R] and 0 <= M - F <= eta pointwise; |E_G M - E_U M| <= eta + K delta. QUANTITATIVE (director): with B = sqrt(t log N), constant eta and q: R = Theta(sqrt(t/log N)), log K = Theta(sqrt(t log N)), log w = Theta(sqrt(t log N)), against Viola/CHMY O(sqrt t log(tq)): a gain of a factor sqrt(log N), so mu >= 0.505 - o(1) remains at t = N^{1.01}. STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE: even with zero cost for the input positions, log K >= R >= t/(B eta) while log w >= B (one block content), so max(log w, log K) >= sqrt(t/eta): compressing positions and states can remove at most the log factor; a polynomial gain needs a decomposition that either does not store a whole block content (log w << B) or has far fewer crossings than t/B - i.e. a different decomposition, not a better encoding of the crossing record. Consistent with JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR seq 17284 (floor log(wK) for term-generic analyses). Novelty not checked; not a gap closure.
PREMISES: CHMY Lemma 19 (TR20-103); Viola, Pseudorandom bits and lower bounds for randomized Turing machines, Sec. 3 (owner check; not local); seq 17284

label: S0193
statement:
ENTROPY-BALANCE (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting: Y uniform on {0,1}^b, x_j = Y_{l(j)} (l surjective, Lupanov-type addressing so that CC(x) <= s for every Y, b = Theta(s log s)); M a correct MCSP[s] DTIME1 machine, accepted set of size <= 2^L, L = O(s log s); A = crossing signature (seq 17306 decomposition), R_alpha = accepted inputs with signature alpha = product of R_{alpha,j} over the block-visit parts J_{alpha,j} (cut-and-paste for a fixed blocking), disjoint over alpha. statement:
ACCEPTANCE-TRIE (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting of seq 17306/17314: for an accepting crossing signature alpha (crossing records include state, time and input-head position), R_alpha = prod_j R_{alpha,j}, a_{alpha,j} = |R_{alpha,j}|, sum_alpha prod_j a_{alpha,j} = A (accepted inputs, disjoint by determinism). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) the trie of R_{alpha,j} has <= a_{alpha,j}+1 nodes per level (reject sink included), so w_{alpha,j} <= min(2^{O(B+log t)}, a_{alpha,j}+1); (ii) the per-alpha ROBP reads the parts J_{alpha,1}, J_{alpha,2}, ... one after another (legitimate: Forbes-Kelley fools arbitrary-order ROBPs) and collapses to accept/reject at part boundaries, so its width is max_j w_{alpha,j}; (iii) splitting each R_{alpha,j} into ceil(a/2^h) pieces of size <= 2^h gives an exact disjoint OR of K'(h) = sum_alpha prod_j ceil(a_{alpha,j}/2^h) ROBPs of width <= 2^h+1, and K'(h) = sum_alpha |R_alpha| 2^{-Phi_h(alpha)} = A E_X[2^{-Phi_h}] (X uniform on accepted inputs), log(w'K') <= h + 1 + log A - P(h). NEW LOWER BOUND (director): ceil(a/2^h) >= 1, so K'(h) >= K_acc := number of accepting signatures with R_alpha nonempty >= 2^{H(alpha(X))} for EVERY distribution X on accepted inputs; hence log(w'K') >= max(h, log K_acc). Replacing prefixes by residual (Myhill-Nerode) classes lowers the width further but leaves K' >= K_acc unchanged. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the trie attacks only point 1 of seq 17306 (width), never point 2 (crossing count); with the floor of seq 17284(2) any success needs s log s >~ log K_acc. (2) With seq 17314 on the Lupanov family: K_acc >= 2^{(rb-L)/(r-1)}, so for multiplicity r > L/b the trie gives no gain over the floor regime. (3) Jensen: P(h) <= E Phi_h <= E sum_j min(h, log a_{alpha,j}) <= E log|R_alpha| = log A - H(alpha(X)). So log(w'K') = N^{o(1)} REQUIRES (a) H(alpha(X)) <= N^{o(1)} and (b) E sum_j min(h, log a_{alpha,j}) >= log A - N^{o(1)} with h = N^{o(1)}: a typical accepted input has >= N^{mu-o(1)} information-carrying parts, each with <= 2^{N^{o(1)}} local completions, while its whole crossing signature has N^{o(1)} bits of entropy, i.e. the accepted set is up to 2^{N^{o(1)}} pieces a union of products with tiny factors and M is almost oblivious on accepted inputs across N^{mu} block visits. (4) The trade-off moves from the block length B to the local acceptance sizes: one block gives K_acc = 1, a = A, log w' = log A, which is exactly seq 17284(2). (5) The folded Cor-17 machine (seq 17279 (c)) is a correct decider, so (a)+(b) fails for it; a proof of (a)+(b) must use q = O(1). label: S0195
statement:
DYNAMIC-CUT + DYNAMIC-CUT-AMORTIZED + FAMILY-CHECKER-CEILING (owner derivations 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (1) DYNAMIC-CUT: in an input-free phase, H(R^1 | R^0, C_c) = 0 (each side evolves from its own content and the crossing states), so H(R^1|R^0), H(L^1|L^0) <= H(C_c) = O(E m_c + 1) for O(1) states, and E T >= Omega(F) - O(|cuts|). Transposition r x r on one tape: F = (r-1) r (r^2-1)/3, T = Omega(b^2). (2) Two-phase check (tape holds y row-major and nothing else, then z is read column-major, accept iff z = y^T): combining the left half of one accepting run with the right half of another with the same crossing protocol (incl. input positions) gives an accepting run on a mixed input, so the left-stored bits read on the right are a function of C; from b = H(Y) <= H(C) + E[b - |S(C)|] follows E|S| <= H(C), both directions E D_c <= 2 H(C_c), H(C_c) = O((E m_c + 1) log b); for every cut in the middle half every column has >= r/4 - O(1) bits on each side, so E m_c = Omega(r) and E T = Omega(b^{3/2}). Section 6 (false acceptances, + 2 lambda) not checked in detail. (3) DYNAMIC-CUT-AMORTIZED: with the same protocol, every left alternative combines with every right alternative to an admissible window alternative, D_j >= a^L a^R, E log a^L >= H(Y_{J^L} | L^0, L^1, C) (injectivity of pi_j; log of the class value count >= conditional entropy), so sum_j (E^L_j + E^R_j) <= Lambda - b. Type: classical crossing-sequence / information-flow arguments (Hennie-type); novelty not checked. STRENGTH (director): the deficits condition on whole half-tape contents; a machine that writes every read input bit onto the tape (O(1) per bit) has L^1, R^1 containing the read bits, so E^L = E^R = 0 for every window and cut. The amortized balance is therefore satisfied at linear cost and yields no time bound by itself; only the flux bound (1) with a forced storage layout gives time, and in the one-way-input model the layout is chosen by the machine (two orders prepared once, 17325). FAMILY-CHECKER-CEILING (director, generalises the exclusion of seq 17325): let F = {x(y)} with x(y)_i = y_{a(i)} for an explicit address map a computable by a size-<=s circuit (every construction used so far: Lupanov addressing seq 17314, permuted repetitions seq 17325, grids). The machine M_F reads y, writes it and the address circuit on the tape, and for each i evaluates a(i) and walks to y_{a(i)}: DTIME1[N (b + poly(s))] = DTIME1[N poly(s)], deterministic, no oracle; it accepts exactly F, |F| = 2^b <= 2^Lambda, and rejects every hybrid. Hence every argument whose premises are 'M accepts F and accepts few inputs / few hybrids' plus machine structure (cut-and-paste, crossing protocols, static or dynamic information flow, any choice of cuts and permutations) proves at most t <= time(M_F) = N s^{c_F}. CHMY Thm 1 needs N^{1.01} for every mu > 0 (its footnote), and N s^{c_F} < N^{1.01} for mu < 0.01/c_F. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): explicit hard-input families with polynomially checkable decoders plus counting plus any cut-and-paste/information-flow analysis, as a route to the magnification hypothesis. A continuation must use acceptance of YES instances outside every such family, i.e. a family whose membership is itself not decidable in DTIME1[N^{1.01}], which is a lower bound of the same kind. PRECISION to seq 17318 (owner): the bound log(w'K') >= max(h, log K_acc) concerns the width budget w' = 2^h+1 and the count of that construction, not the width of every realised ROBP; the entropy bound K_acc >= 2^{H(alpha(X))} is unrestricted. Not a gap closure.

label: S0196
statement:
UCC STRENGTH CHECK (owner proposal 'UNIFORM COMPUTATION COMPRESSION' 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Owner's quantitative target confirmed: under P = NP, MMW/CHMY give T(N, N^mu) <= N^{1+c mu} for a fixed unknown c, so a bound T(N, N^mu) >= N^{1+delta} with fixed delta for all small mu is sufficient (consistent with seq 17325/17328: no bound of the form N s^{c'} with fixed c' suffices). (1) UCC => P != NP: verified (P = NP => Q in DTIME(m^c) => every L_k in DTIME(n^{a max(1,c)}), contradicting the time hierarchy for k > a max(1,c)). (2) EQUIVALENT FORM: UCC <=> there are j, b with P contained in Sigma_j TIME(n^b) (=>: Q in Sigma_j TIME(m^d) composed with R_k; <=: Sigma_j-SAT is complete for Sigma_j TIME(n^b) under n^b polylog-time reductions). So UCC asserts a polynomial speedup of ARBITRARY degree of deterministic time by bounded alternation; it implies P != PH. No such speedup is known (known for multitape TMs: constant-factor / log-factor alternation speedups such as Paul-Pippenger-Szemeredi-Trotter). (3) RANDOM-ORACLE SEPARATION: for a random oracle A, P^A != NP^A with probability 1 (Bennett-Gill), but UCC^A fails with probability 1: L^A = parity of A on the first n^k strings is in DTIME^A(n^{k+1}); a Sigma_j TIME^A(n^b) machine is a depth-(j+1) circuit of size 2^{O(n^b)} with bottom fan-in n^b over these n^k oracle bits, which by Hastad's correlation bound agrees with parity on a negligible fraction once k > b j (+O(1)); countably many machines. Hence UCC is strictly stronger than P != NP in the relativised sense, and any proof must be non-relativising and must fail in a world where P != NP holds. CLASSIFICATION under the owner rule of 2026-11-26: a new conditional chain whose antecedent implies P != NP; it does not shrink an existing gap; not adopted as a FruitStack target unless the owner overrides. Not a gap closure.

label: S0198
statement:
MMW-SWEEP (owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: a one-pass streaming algorithm with space S and update time U is simulated by a one-tape machine with one-way input whose head pattern is input-independent (read one bit at the left end, then exactly U full forward/backward sweeps over the O(S)-cell configuration, one local cellular update per sweep pair, padded): T = O(N S U). With MMW Thm 1.3 and s(n) = n^2: P = NP implies MCSP[n^2] in sweep-DTIME1[N (log N)^{O(1)}]. This is CHMY Thm 47 (proof via MMW Thm 1.3 + Lemma 9, any time-constructible s) at s = n^2 plus an oblivious normal form. LOGICAL STRENGTH: a sweep machine with time T does r sweeps of W cells per bit, T >= N r W, so it is a one-pass streaming algorithm with space O(W) and update O(rW); conversely the construction above. Hence 'MCSP[n^2] not in sweep-DTIME1[N (log N)^{omega(1)}]' is polynomially equivalent to 'MCSP[n^2] has no deterministic streaming algorithm with polylog space and polylog update', which is MMW's own headline target (mmw19 paper.txt l.100-104: an N poly(log N)-time lower bound on poly(log N)-space streaming for MCSP[n^c] is as hard as P != NP) and the QE*/L* target of seq 10055 (G0004/G0012). It is a normal form of the existing target, not a gap shrink; restricting to oblivious machines yields no easier model here. CORRECTION ACCEPTED (owner): obliviousness fixes crossing times, positions and directions, not the transmitted states; condition (a) of seq 17318 is not automatic (the director's earlier remark was wrong). BARRIERS that apply unchanged: (i) MMW Thm 1.2 / CHMY Lemma 16 give unconditionally a streaming algorithm with O~(s) space, O~(s^2) update and Sigma3-oracle queries of length O~(s) = polylog N, and it has the same sweep form, so any proof must fail for sweep machines with polylog-length Sigma3 queries; (ii) seq 17328 checker ceiling: family-plus-counting arguments give at most N s^{c_F} = N (log N)^{O(1)} with a fixed exponent, while the target needs exponent omega(1). Not a gap closure.
